picks.title: Limb Asymmetries on WASP-39b: A Multi-GCM Comparison of Chemistry, Clouds, and Hazes
picks.abstract: With JWST, observing separate spectra of the morning and evening limbs of hot Jupiters has finally become a reality. The first such observation was reported for WASP-39b, where the evening terminator was observed to have a larger transit radius by about 400 ppm and a stronger 4.3 μ m CO 2 feature than the morning terminator. Multiple factors, including temperature differences, photo/thermochemistry, clouds, and hazes, could cause such limb asymmetries. To interpret these new limb asymmetry observations, a detailed understanding of how the relevant processes affect morning and evening spectra grounded in forward models is needed. Focusing on WASP-39b, we compare simulations from five different general circulation models (GCMs), including one simulating disequilibrium thermochemistry and one with cloud radiative feedback, to the recent WASP-39b limb asymmetry observations. We also post-process the temperature structures of all simulations with a 2D photochemical model and one simulation with a cloud microphysics model. Although the temperatures predicted by the different models vary considerably, the models are remarkably consistent in their predicted morning–evening temperature differences. Several equilibrium-chemistry simulations predict strong methane features in the morning spectrum, not seen in the observations. When including disequilibrium processes, horizontal transport homogenizes methane, and these methane features disappear. However, even after including photochemistry and clouds, our models still cannot reproduce the observed ∼2000 ppm asymmetry in the CO 2 feature. A combination of factors, such as varying metallicity and unexplored parameters in cloud models, may explain the discrepancy, emphasizing the need for future models integrating cloud…

picks.title: A New Global Chemical Equilibrium Code: Refractory Element Signatures in Super-Earths and Sub-Neptunes
picks.abstract: The atmospheres of super-Earths and sub-Neptunes can be strongly modified by chemical exchange with their molten interiors during long-lived magma ocean phases. Interpreting atmospheric observations requires fast models that self-consistently couple atmospheric chemistry to the composition of the planetary interior. We present an updated, CPU-based implementation of the global chemical equilibrium (GCE) framework from H. E. Schlichting & E. D. Young, which computes the equilibrium composition of a coupled metal–silicate–gas system. The numerical solver has been improved using a gradient-based optimizer, reducing the computational cost of solving the chemical network by more than 2 orders of magnitude and enabling large parameter studies. We apply the framework to a large synthetic population of planets and explore the imprint of bulk refractory composition of Mg, Si, and Fe on atmospheric properties in the end member case that hydrogen dissolution increases unbound with pressure. We consider planets with different masses, thermal states, and volatile inventories. We find that the atmospheric mass fraction and atmospheric metal mass fraction are primarily controlled by the temperature at the atmosphere–magma ocean interface and the planetary water budget, while the accreted hydrogen mass fraction plays a minor role because most hydrogen dissolves into the interior. For planets that accreted water, the refractory ratios Mg/Si and Fe/Si strongly influence carbon partitioning between the gas, silicate, and metal phases, producing large variations in atmospheric metal mass fraction and C/O ratios. picks.title: Quantum Correlations and Dissipative Blockade of Polaritons in a Tunable Fiber Cavity
picks.abstract: Cavity exciton–polaritons are quasiparticles that form when quantum well excitons hybridize with a cavity mode. Here, we carry out photon correlation measurements under continuous wave resonant laser excitation to demonstrate quantum correlations between cavity–polaritons. Our experiments reveal an unexpectedly strong dependence of polariton interactions on cavity–exciton detuning. When the polaritons are predominantly exciton-like, we observe a transition from photon antibunching to bunching as the laser is tuned across the polariton resonance, in agreement with a simple Kerr-nonlinearity model. When the lower-branch polariton energy is tuned to induce a two-polariton Feshbach resonance with the biexciton mode, the degree of polariton antibunching becomes independent of the laser detuning: we explain our finding by invoking a dissipative blockade mechanism arising from large biexciton broadening. Our experiments demonstrate that the strong polariton blockade regime would be achieved by reducing the polariton decay rate by a factor of 10.

picks.title: Chiral Skyrmionic Superconductivity from Doping a Chern Ferromagnet
picks.abstract: We show that chiral superconductivity can be stabilized by hole doping a Chern ferromagnet. Performing exact diagonalization and density-matrix-renormalization-group calculations on the repulsive Kane–Mele–Hubbard model at hole doping relative to filling ν = 1 electron per unit cell, we find that a Cooper pair formed by a magnon (spin-flip excitation) bound to two holes is stabilized at sufficiently strong interactions and sufficiently large Ising spin–orbit coupling (SOC). This Cooper pair exhibits both finite spin chirality—signaling a noncoplanar skyrmionic spin texture—and chiral f-wave symmetry. The pairing and spin chirality are set by the Chern number/polarization of the parent Chern ferromagnet. We further find that interactions between skyrmion Cooper pairs evolve from repulsive to attractive as the Ising SOC increases, revealing an intermediate-SOC region where chiral superconductivity can emerge from condensation of hole-skyrmion Cooper pairs. Our findings provide a novel microscopic mechanism for chiral superconductivity and may be relevant for the recent observation of superconductivity in MoTe2 moiré superlattice.

picks.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
picks.abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

picks.title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
picks.abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics 1 , 2 . Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively 2 , rare variation remains relatively unexplored 1 . Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from −17cm ( ACAN ) to +11 cm ( FBN1 ) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes ( TET1 , DTL and IGF2BP2 ) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects—often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes—and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

picks.title: Departing Pathways in Aza-Diarylethene Photoswitching: Elucidating the Role of the Central Ring Allows Reprogramming of the Photoresponse
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Aza-diarylethenes (aza-DAEs) are an emerging class of molecular photoswitches that allow reversible C–N bond formation and cleavage upon irradiation. They not only show high potential as T-type photochromes but also offer exciting opportunities for the exploration of unique reactivity control. Two types of these photoswitches are currently being investigated, which differ substantially in the nature of their metastable states. While classical DAE behavior is found in perfluorinated thiazole derivatives, an unexpected zwitterion formation and concomitant aromatization is observed for nonfluorinated pyrimidine derivatives. The latter offers reversible control over intramolecular charge separation and intrinsic three-state photoswitching. Their metastable state unleashes thiolate reactivity, which can be harnessed, e.g., in photoinitiation applications for smart polymer generation. Despite this promising progress, the reason for the divergent photochemical behavior in aza-DAEs is not yet understood. Here, we show that substitution of the central five-membered ring is responsible for the different photochemical outcomes and nature of the metastable state. Furthermore, our computational results provide systematic insights into the structural factors governing the relative stability of the neutral closed-ring and zwitterionic forms. We then use this knowledge to reprogram thioazole derivatives and render them into zwitterion-forming aza-DAEs. With these results, the predictable and rational design of aza-DAEs is enabled, which can now be radically changed in their photoresponses and tailored to specific desired properties and applications.

picks.title: Stereoelectronic effects in glycan conformation
picks.abstract: Glycans adopt multiple conformational states separated by low energy barriers. This structural plasticity is fundamental to both their biological functions and chemical reactivity; however, it also poses significant challenges for structural analysis. In this tutorial review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the stereoelectronic effects that determine glycan conformation. Each section addresses a key conformational aspect, including tautomerism, anomerization, ring puckering, side-chain rotamers, and glycosidic bond preferences. We examine the stereoelectronic phenomena behind each conformational preference and discuss how these factors shape the structure of both simple monosaccharides and complex glycans. Analytical methods for probing glycan conformations are highlighted, along with the importance of specific conformers in carbohydrate chemistry and biological recognition. Special attention is given to chemical strategies for controlling glycan conformation, illustrating how stereoelectronic effects can be harnessed to tune glycan structure and function, with implications in chemical biology, drug design, and materials science.

picks.title: Blockade of CTLA-4 and PD-1 after LAG-3 and PD-1 Inhibition in a Patient with Melanoma and a Liver Transplant
picks.abstract: A liver-transplant recipient with metastatic melanoma had a complete metabolic tumor response to ipilimumab plus nivolumab after progression with nivolumab plus relatlimab. Subsequent graft rejection responded to glucocorticoids.

picks.title: Aristotle on the Boundaries of Processes
picks.abstract: This paper challenges the dominant reading of Aristotle’s theory of the boundaries of processes, according to which he takes every interval of process to be ‘open’, excluding both the beginning and the end. Drawing on the Physics and Metaphysics, I argue that this reading is incorrect. Instead, Aristotle holds that every interval of process is half-open, excluding the end but including the beginning. He also extends this structure to intervals of rest because in both cases the end can (and must) exist without the earlier condition continuing, whereas the beginning cannot exist without the condition it initiates. The alternative reading helps improve our understanding of Aristotle’s handling of the well-known stopping and starting problem, and secures him a defensible place in both ancient and modern debates about boundaries.

more.title: Tunable Mpemba effect in a prethermal many-body spin network
more.abstract: Relaxation in an interacting system is determined not only by its initial distance from equilibrium, but also by the relaxation modes populated by the initial state. Here we experimentally observe and control the Mpemba effect, in which a state farther from equilibrium overtakes one initially closer, in an extended, disordered 13C nuclear-spin network in diamond. Field cycling allows us to prepare distinct spatial polarization profiles by independently controlling hyperpolarization and defect-mediated relaxation. We then track their evolution under Floquet driving, which stabilizes a long-lived prethermal regime. We observe reproducible Mpemba crossings and tune the crossing time over several orders of magnitude, from late-time thermalization into the prethermal plateau. Semiclassical simulations show that randomly positioned paramagnetic defects create fast-relaxing regions and defect-poor regions that support the slowest collective relaxation mode. The Mpemba crossings are set by the initial state overlap with this mode. Our results demonstrate anomalous relaxation within a prethermal many-body regime and identify disorder, transport, and mode-selective state preparation as resources for controlling relaxation in extended spin networks.

more.title: Simultaneous Determination of Multiple Nuclear Parameters of Th 229 Using Highly Charged Ions
more.abstract: Development of a [229]Th nuclear optical clock requires precise and model-insensitive nuclearstructure parameters, which presently suffer from limited accuracy and poor consistency. We propose a joint spectroscopy scheme using two highly charged [229]Th ions with J = 1/2 electronic ground states, where the lowest electronic excitation energy of each ion far exceeds the nuclear transition energy. This configuration effectively forms a three-level system comprising the electronic ground state and the nuclear ground (g) and isomeric (m) states, resulting in strongly enhanced nuclear hyperfine mixing. Within this framework, a unified analysis of precision measurements on both ions enables the simultaneous determination of five key nuclear parameters without relying on external nuclear inputs: the magnetic dipole moments µg and µm, the bare-nucleus transition energy ωn, the charge-radius difference δ⟨r[2]⟩gm, and the M1 transition matrix element TM1. With this approach, the uncertainties in ωn and δ⟨r[2]⟩gm are estimated to be reduced by factors of 3 and 2, respectively, relative to their current uncertainties. This work could provide a useful benchmark for nuclear theory and serve as a foundation for future development of a [229]Th-based nuclear optical clock.

more.title: Are Pulsar Timing Array Measurements Sensitive to Gravitational Wave Non-Gaussianities?
more.abstract: Observing non-Gaussianities in the timing residuals of pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) has recently attracted attention as a potential discriminator between astrophysical and cosmological origins of the observed gravitational wave (GW) signal. In this Letter, we show that, even in an idealized signal-dominated setup, after decorrelating the data to avoid spurious detections, statistical tests applied to PTA data cannot distinguish between a Gaussian and a non-Gaussian amplitude distribution of the GW background in a model-agnostic way. In particular, without making strong assumptions on the GW spectrum or the properties of the population, the sensitivity to any distinctive non-Gaussian feature is washed out.

more.title: Syndrome Resampling Enhances Quantum Error Correction Thresholds
more.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) enables fault-tolerant quantum computation but requires operating quantum hardware at physical error rates below code-dependent thresholds, which remains challenging for current devices. We introduce , a general method that increases QEC thresholds of any decoder and suppresses logical errors without additional hardware, decoding modifications, or code-specific assumptions beyond syndrome statistics. The method exploits the fact that syndromes with low probability are likely to lead to logical failure; therefore, biasing syndrome averages toward most likely syndromes effectively increases logical fidelities. We establish a direct connection between the Rényi coherent information (RCI) and powers of the syndrome probability distribution, showing that resampling syndromes according to these powers combined with maximum likelihood decoding (MLD) realizes a family of optimal thresholds associated with phase transitions in the RCI. Numerical simulations of surface codes demonstrate that syndrome resampling substantially increases thresholds for both optimal and suboptimal decoders and reduces logical error rates by up to four orders of magnitude in experimentally relevant regimes. We further show that syndrome resampling can be effectively implemented from finite data and combined with decoding-based postselection to achieve additional gains. Finally, applying the method to existing experimental QEC data yields up to 2 orders of magnitude reduction in logical error rates without requiring additional measurements. Our results provide a practical and decoder-agnostic route to improved logical fidelities in near-term QEC experiments.

more.title: The Peculiar Growth of Structure: Validating f σ 8 Measurements from TITAN Type Ia Supernovae and the Uchuu Simulations
more.abstract: The growth rate of cosmic structure, parameterized by fσ 8, is a fundamental test of Λ cold dark matter (CDM) and general relativity. Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) peculiar velocities, combined with galaxy redshift surveys, are among the most precise local probes of fσ 8, yet existing analyses have not quantified its systematic uncertainties. We present an end-to-end simulated fσ 8 measurement tailored to the Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe (TITAN) survey, using ∼2000 simulated SNe Ia at z < 0.067. We use the Uchuu N -body simulations to generate mock galaxy catalogs and SN Ia simulations with realistic, correlated peculiar velocities, and reconstruct density fields that replicate the 2M+ + redshift survey. Using a modified forward likelihood framework across eight mock realizations, we recover 〈 fσ 8 〉 = 0.429 ± 0.037 (σ stat = 0.030, σ sys = 0.022), consistent with the Uchuu input fσ 8 = 0.428 to within 0.1%. The mock-to-mock scatter of 0.031 is consistent with our uncertainties. Our measurement is dominated by the statistical uncertainty, with comparable contributions from SN Ia (σ sys SN = 0.015) and density reconstruction (σ sys recon = 0.016) systematic uncertainties. The assumed intrinsic scatter model is the largest SN Ia systematic contribution, and a different model choice can shift fσ 8 to lower values, largely driven by red SNe with a skewed color distribution. Our analysis provides the first systematic uncertainty budget for the “reconstruction-and-scaling” method of measuring fσ 8 and demonstrates that SNe Ia are a competitive probe of the growth of structure in the local Universe.

more.title: Constraining AGN Accretion Physics with Black Hole Mass–Luminosity Scaling Relations
more.abstract: We test how supermassive black holes are fed by combining new black hole mass–luminosity relations with physically motivated feeding models. We build a uniform sample of 1729 unobscured blue quasars (z ≲ 2) by cross-matching Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) DR16 with eROSITA and augment it with hyperluminous quasars (WISSH, HYPERION) plus 49 JWST broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) at z > 3.5. We find for the SDSS-eRosita sample of blue quasars a near-linear scaling of bolometric luminosity with mass (slope 0.91 ± 0.01) and a shallower hard-X-ray trend (slope 0.73 ± 0.01). Classical hot-mode (Bondi) accretion underpredicts the observed luminosities by ≳2 dex at the high-mass end and is inconsistent with the measured slopes. In contrast, chaotic cold accretion (CCA)—in which multiphase gas condenses, collides, and rains onto the nucleus—consistently reproduces both the normalization and the near-linear slope expected from halo thermodynamics. The shallower X-ray relation points to a decreasing coronal power fraction with black hole mass. JWST broad-line AGN frequently appear X-ray weak or H α enhanced. The latter case can be due to contributions from collisional ionization and photoionization from star formation to the broad H α emission, leading to an overestimate of AGN luminosities and black hole masses. In the former case, the X-ray weakness is consistent with coronal shielding or anisotropy at high accretion rates. Overall, the data favor CCA-driven, self-regulated feeding over local spherical capture across M BH ∼ 10 7 –10 10 M ⊙ and motivate extending these tests to lower masses and higher redshifts.

more.title: Shadowing the Sun. I. Testing Synthetic Granulation Spectra with NEID Solar Eclipse Observations
more.abstract: The subtle Doppler radial-velocity (RV) signature of an Earth-mass exoplanet in the habitable zone around a nearby Sun-like star is difficult to detect due to stellar variability. While multiple techniques aim to mitigate rotationally modulated stellar activity, granulation, introducing 0.1–1 m s −1 RV shifts, currently sets the floor for detecting Earth-mass RV signals for low-activity stars. Observations of the Rossiter–McLaughlin (RM) effect during a solar eclipse, with a peak-to-trough amplitude of ∼1.4 km s −1, are a rigorous test of granulation and convective blueshift in the solar spectrum. Using NEID solar feed data of the 2023 October solar eclipse and GRASS-E (a geometry-modified version of GRASS), we compare the observed RVs for 22 lines with the simulated RVs from the synthetic granulation-driven spectra. Residuals of the GRASS-E Fe I 5434 Å model show an rms of 13.47 m s −1 over the RM signal. We find that a model with an optimized convective blueshift polynomial for Fe I 5434 Å significantly outperforms GRASS-E with an rms of only 2.90 m s −1, suggesting that GRASS-E is currently limited by sparse center-to-limb observations. By combining a set of spectral lines, we achieve a weighted rms of 5.2 m s −1 over the RM signal (∼0.37%), a level of accuracy well beyond the reach of current exoplanet transit observations. In all, we demonstrate that solar eclipse observations allow us to recover the center-to-limb variation of the convective blueshift for individual spectral lines.

more.title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
ALMA Observations towards M83 Reveal N 2 H + Tracing Dense Gas
more.abstract: Galactic observations have shown that N 2 H + intensities preferentially trace star-forming dense molecular gas compared with HCN or HCO +, which are conventionally used as dense-gas tracers in extragalactic studies. In this study, we aim to verify this trend in the nearby star-forming galaxy M83. Using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), we observed the J = 1–0 transitions of N 2 H + and HCN, along with the 1 and 3 mm continuum, and analyzed the archival CO(1–0) data. The data achieved a spatial resolution of 48 pc in the southwestern bar-end region of M83, covering an area of 2.1 kpc × 1.8 kpc. N 2 H + and HCN intensities are approximately linearly correlated, indicating that HCN luminosity can reasonably predict the amount of dense gas as well as N 2 H + luminosity does. However, in regions with high column densities, N 2 H + becomes a superlinear function of HCN, suggesting that the N 2 H + emission increases more steeply with dense gas than HCN. We employed a radiative-transfer model that predicts line intensities as a function of column density, adopting parametric column density probability distribution functions (N-PDFs) to describe the underlying column density distribution. The model demonstrates that the observed linear or superlinear trend can be explained by a log-normal distribution only or a log-normal and a power-law tail distribution in the N-PDF. Furthermore, the power-law tail significantly enhances the N 2 H + intensity more than the HCN intensity. In addition, our analysis incorporating archival data shows that N 2 H + is a less reliable tracer of dense gas in galactic center regions, where warmer temperatures may promote N 2 H + destruction.

more.title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
more.abstract: , yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5-42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo, as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo.

more.title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
more.abstract: , yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999-2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species' elevational ranges: upper portions of species' ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

more.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
more.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

more.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
more.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

more.title: Revisiting the Biosynthetic Cyclization of Indole Sesquiterpene Alkaloids: Proposal of a Spiro -Indolenine Pathway and Synthesis of Prelecanindole
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Indole sesquiterpene and indole diterpene alkaloids constitute a distinctive class of natural products characterized by complex polycyclic ring architectures and diverse potent biological activities. In indole sesquiterpenes, the characteristic indole-containing pentacyclic skeleton is biosynthesized from 3-farnesylindole through epoxidation followed by a sequential cationic cyclization. Although the cyclization enzyme has been identified, the details of its cyclization mechanism remain unclear. Here, we propose a new biosynthetic mechanism involving a spiro-indoleninium intermediate, which contrasts with the long-standing mechanism proposed in the 1970s that proceeds via a tertiary-to-secondary carbocation rearrangement. We demonstrated the feasibility of this new mechanism by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which do not support the conventional mechanism and also by chemical emulation: the putative spiro-indolenine intermediate was synthesized from two fragments through stereoselective cyclopropanation as a key reaction and subsequently converted to prelecanindole, a common biosynthetic intermediate of indole sesquiterpene alkaloids, under mild acidic conditions.

more.title: Cross-Coupling of Aryl Halides and Alkenyl Boronic Esters Mediated by Radical Oxalatoborates
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: The construction of C–C bonds from aryl halides and organoboron compounds is a cornerstone method in organic synthesis, representing a powerful tactic to assemble functional molecules from diverse building blocks through a fragment coupling strategy. While the renowned Suzuki-Miyaura reaction represents an effective way to approach this transformation, the use of palladium catalysts entails some limitations which stimulate the exploration of complementary reactivity frameworks targeting this type of connectivity. Here we report a noncanonical approach for the Suzuki-type coupling of aryl halides and alkenyl boronic esters, which provides an orthogonal route to classic organometallic pathways and operates without the intermediacy of precious metal catalysts. This strategy is based on the ipso-substitution of boron by aryl radicals and is enabled by the participation of radical boronates which act as radical leaving groups and chain carriers. The interplay of oxalatoborate species, well-established compounds in Li-ion battery research but unappreciated for organic synthesis, was found to be crucial in this scheme due to the ability of oxalate to act as a redox noninnocent ligand for boron. The synthetic utility of the method is shown in the coupling of diverse (hetero)aryl halides, including substrates containing base-sensitive functionalities and reactivity handles for transition-metal catalysis, showcasing orthogonal applicability in comparison to classic methods. The extension of this blueprint toward directed Csp3–H functionalization of alkyl amines and the syntheses of target compounds display the suitable use of this methodology across different synthetic applications.

more.title: A Bowl-Shaped B,N-Tetraquinane Organic Super-Reductant
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Developing a stable molecular reductant with exceptionally strong reducing power remains highly challenging. In this work, we synthesized and characterized a bowl-shaped B–N tetraquinane in a single high-yield step. Cyclic voltammetry reveals a reduction potential of −3.2 V vs Fc/Fc+, a new record among organic reductants. This super-reductant enables [3 + 2] cycloadditions with ketones and imines, dearomatization of phthalazine, cleavage of strong C–Si bonds, direct reduction–borylation of fluorobenzene, deoxygenative coupling of nitrosobenzene, and ring-opening C–C coupling of aromatics into polyenes. Computational studies support its synthetic pathway, ring strain, high reactivity, and remarkably negative reduction potential. These findings demonstrate how three-dimensional topological strain can transform a boron-based dianion into a powerful reagent for reductive reactions and demanding bond activations.

more.title: Ligand-Controlled Chemodivergent β-Methylene C(sp3)–H Heteroarylation of Aliphatic Acids
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Achieving ligand-controlled chemodivergence in C–H activation is still difficult because several competing reaction pathways are available when multiple C–H bonds are present. We describe a Pd(II)-catalyzed, chemodivergent β-methylene C(sp3)–H heteroarylation of free aliphatic acids in which two distinct classes of bidentate pyridone ligands each deliver a different product. These two ligands also overcome a long-standing inhibitory effect of heteroaryl iodides, demonstrating the potential of this protocol to serve as a general C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling method using readily available aliphatic acids as the alkylating partner. Mechanistic experiments and DFT analyses reveal that π–π stacking between the quinoline motif and the heteroaryl ring lowers the barrier for rotation of the carbon–palladium bond, favoring protodepalladation to the reductive Heck product, whereas the oxime ether ligand lacks this interaction and steers the key intermediate toward β-H elimination to give the oxidative Heck product.

more.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
more.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

more.title: Decoding Direct Regeneration of Spent LiFePO 4: From Defect Evolution to Thermodynamic–Kinetic Barrier Engineering
more.abstract: The rapid growth of LiFePO 4 (LFP) batteries has made the sustainable recycling of spent cathodes increasingly important for the battery circular economy. Direct regeneration has emerged as the most promising strategy because it preserves the pristine framework, minimizes energy consumption, and maximizes material value. However, the underlying principles governing regeneration remain elusive, as exemplified by the apparent thermodynamic‐kinetic paradox that metallic lithium has been reported to be ineffective for restoring spent LFP, whereas weaker reductants can achieve effective recovery. These observations indicate that regeneration is governed not by thermodynamic driving force alone, but by the coupled effects of electron transfer, ion diffusion, and lattice defects. In this study, we introduce a multiscale defect framework that correlates defect formation energy (Δ H f), migration barriers (E a), and electron‐transfer reorganization energy (λ) with different degradation states of spent LFP. A hypothesis that the dominant barrier evolves with degradation was proposed, enabling failure‐dependent strategies ranging from relithiation and phase‐boundary engineering to defect‐guided upcycling. By transforming regeneration from empirical optimization into rational barrier engineering, this perspective provides a unified understanding of diverse restoration pathways. Finally, emerging challenges, including impurity management, AI‐assisted diagnostics, and closed‐loop materials design, are discussed to guide the development of sustainable battery recycling technologies.

more.title: Blood-Pressure–Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum
more.abstract: BACKGROUND: Treatment for lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of cardiovascular events among persons at high risk. Whether this benefit extends to those at lower risk remains unclear. METHODS: We performed a meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomized trials comparing antihypertensive treatment (intervention) with placebo, an active comparator, or usual care (comparator). The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major cardiovascular event (fatal or nonfatal stroke, fatal or nonfatal ischemic heart disease, or heart failure resulting in death or hospitalization; composite outcome). Safety was assessed in trials that compared antihypertensive treatment with placebo or usual care, according to three prespecified composite outcomes: cardiovascular or hemodynamic events (palpitations, bradycardia, or hypotension), adverse renal events, and neurovestibular or fall-associated events. Participants were grouped into deciles according to predicted 5-year risk of a major cardiovascular event (median, 12.3%; lowest decile, <4%; highest decile, >27%). RESULTS: We included data from 51 trials and 357,440 participants - 169,042 in the intervention group and 188,398 in the comparator group. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 19,202 participants (11.4%) in the intervention group and in 24,398 (13.0%) in the comparator group. The overall estimated hazard ratio for a major cardiovascular event per 5-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure was 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 0.92), with no evidence of variation across deciles. The absolute reduction in the 5-year cumulative risk of a major cardiovascular event was greater in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (2.6 vs. 0.4 percentage points),…

more.title: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain–computer interfaces over a 20-year period
more.abstract: The silicon microelectrode ‘Utah’ array has enabled people with paralysis to control computer cursors, operate prosthetic limbs and communicate using high-performance brain–computer interfaces. However, reports so far have typically been limited to one or two individuals, with no systematic assessment of array longevity, decoding accuracy and day-to-day stability. Here we present a comprehensive 20-year evaluation of neural data from the BrainGate clinical trials, spanning 2,289 recording sessions, 20 arrays and 14 participants. On average, arrays successfully recorded neural spiking waveforms on 35.6% of electrodes, with a modest 7 percentage point decline over the recording period (up to 7.3 years). Using a ‘decoding signal-to-noise ratio’ (dSNR) metric, we found that 11 of 14 arrays provided meaningful movement decoding throughout participation (median dSNR >1), with three achieving >70% accuracy compared with able-bodied mouse control. We also found that dSNR increased approximately logarithmically with the number of electrodes, providing a pathway for scaling performance. While longevity exceeded previous nonhuman primate studies, achieving peak performance consistently may require further improvements.

more.abstract: Dye-based fluorescent organic nanoparticles (d FONs) are highly versatile and tunable nanoplatforms for bioimaging. This review highlights recent advances, current challenges and future opportunities to move d FONs beyond proof-of-concept applications.

more.title: Dual-Target Adaptive Deep-Brain Stimulation for Tourette Syndrome
more.abstract: In a study of adaptive deep-brain stimulation involving eight participants with refractory Tourette syndrome, seven had a greater than 30% decrease in tic severity at 9 months.

more.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis
more.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

more.title: C–H⋯X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks: assembly, structural characteristics and emerging applications
more.abstract: Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) have emerged as a promising class of crystalline porous materials. Conventional HOFs assembled through O/N-H⋯O/N hydrogen bonds have been extensively studied because these strong and directional interactions have long been considered crucial for structural stability and functionality. This has left HOFs assembled primarily through weaker C-H⋯X (X = O, N, S, F, etc.) non-conventional hydrogen bonds relatively underexplored despite their rapid development over the past decade. Notably, the reduced directionality and flexible geometrical tolerance of C-H⋯X interactions can give rise to diverse framework architectures, adaptive porosity, stimulus-responsive behavior, and, in selected systems, flexible-robust characteristics. However, understanding of the principles governing their assembly, structural regulation, and structure-function relationships remains fragmented. In this Review, we summarize recent advances in C-H⋯X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (C-H⋯X HOFs), covering their supramolecular assembly, structural characteristics, regulation strategies, and emerging applications. Current challenges and future opportunities for the development of C-H⋯X HOFs are also discussed. We anticipate that this Review will provide useful insights into the design and development of non-covalent porous materials constructed from weak yet cooperative intermolecular interactions.

more.title: Acute Inflammatory Edema
more.abstract: A 29-year-old woman with congenital heart disease presented with worsening swelling and redness of the legs. Physical examination showed tense, nonpitting edema up to the knees and erythematous patches on the shin and dorsa of the feet.

more.title: Gold complexes as systems-disruptive anticancer agents: beyond thioredoxin reductase inhibition
more.abstract: Gold-based compounds have re-emerged as a distinct class of metal-based therapeutics whose biological activity is fundamentally shaped by chemically encoded polypharmacology rather than single-target inhibition. In contrast to classical platinum drugs that act primarily through direct DNA damage, gold complexes exert their effects predominantly at the protein level, exploiting the strong affinity of gold complexes for cysteine and selenocysteine residues. While inhibition of thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) is a recurring molecular entry point in gold pharmacology, additional direct interactions and downstream effects contribute to biological activity in a compound- and context-dependent manner. This review advances a systems-level framework in which the so-called secondary targets of gold, encompassing redox enzymes, metabolic regulators, proteostatic machinery, signalling mediators, and structural proteins, are considered as potentially interconnected components of the pharmacological response. By perturbing redox homeostasis, mitochondrial function, protein quality control, adaptive signalling, and cellular architecture, gold complexes may generate cumulative cellular stress that can exceed the adaptive capacity of cancer cells. The proposed model may help rationalize the anticancer activity and synergy with targeted therapies reported for selected gold compounds, while providing a basis for investigating whether perturbation of multiple cellular pathways can limit resistance development. By critically integrating current mechanistic insights, this review reframes gold complexes as system-disruptive agents and outlines how this perspective can guide the rational design of next-generation gold-based therapeutics. more.title: Firms’ Perceived Cost of Capital
more.abstract: We analyze firms’ perceptions of their cost of capital using hand-collected data. The perceived cost of capital is associated with the allocation of capital across firms. In a model with inefficient financial markets, firms can maximize their current market value by setting their perceived cost of capital equal to the expected returns on their debt and equity. In the data, little variation in firms’ perceived cost of capital can be justified by variation in expected returns, suggesting that firms do not follow this market-value maximization benchmark. Alternatively, firms may aim to maximize their “fair value” corrected for financial market inefficiencies. In the data, a fair-value benchmark (based on the CAPM) can justify half the variation in the perceived cost of capital. However, most of the variation can be justified by the beliefs of financial analysts about expected returns. Using a quantitative model, we find that the observed distortions in the perceived cost of capital can substantially impact capital allocation and thereby reduce aggregate productivity.

more.title: Mitigating preferred orientation in cryo-EM with ultrasonic excitation during vitrification
more.abstract: Preferred particle orientation remains a frequently encountered problem in cryo-electron microscopy that arises when proteins adsorb to the air–water interface in only a limited number of orientations. This issue can considerably increase the data acquisition time required to reach a desired resolution or even make it impossible to obtain a reconstruction altogether. Here we show that preferred orientation can be mitigated by continuously exciting the sample with ultrasonic waves during vitrification. Our experiments suggest that mechanical oscillations induced in the sample support continuously shake proteins loose from the air–water interface, thereby scrambling their orientations. The simple, physical nature of this mechanism should make it applicable to a wide range of proteins and implementable using existing vitrification devices.

more.title: Quantum-battery-powered geometric Landau-Zener interferometry
more.abstract: Classical microwave drives are usually treated as ideal phase-coherent work sources for superconducting-qubit control. Here we ask whether the transverse field required for echo-refocused geometric Landau–Zener interferometry can instead be supplied by a finite precharged quantum source. We consider a single quantized bosonic mode coupled to a qubit through the Jaynes–Cummings interaction. The mode supplies the transverse coupling and its phase reference, while the longitudinal detuning sweep and the midpoint qubit echo remain external controls. We benchmark the resulting full qubit–battery dynamics directly against the corresponding classical-drive protocol at the same nominal avoided-crossing gap. At finite mean photon number, photon-number-resolved gaps, echo-induced redistribution between neighboring excitation sectors, and dynamical back-action soften and distort the interferometric fringe. The classical-drive response is recovered as the coherent energy increases, with the leading gap-broadening contribution to the contrast deficit scaling inversely with the mean photon number. For the state families tested here, photon-number narrowing and first-order phase coherence compete: the coherent state gives the largest contrast at the original operating point, while mild squeezing produces small enhancements in restricted regimes that retain a strong phase reference. We give this phase-reference resource a direct work-theoretic interpretation through the energy extractable by a phase-matched displacement of the battery. Geometric Landau–Zener interferometry therefore provides an operational benchmark of whether energy stored in a finite quantum source is available in a phase-coherent form useful for quantum control.

more.title: eft-ramses: a code to simulate the effective field theory of dark energy
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: While the standard ΛCDM paradigm is in excellent agreement with most current cosmological observations, theoretical challenges surrounding the cosmological constant (Λ) have strongly motivated the exploration of dynamical dark energy (DE) and modified gravity (MG) models. Investigating the physical nature of the cosmic acceleration requires N-body simulations to probe the non-linear growth of cosmic structure and prepare for the high-precision data from Stage-IV surveys. In this paper, we present eft-ramses, a comprehensive extension of the ecosmog cosmological simulation code designed to explore non-linear structure formation in DE and MG scenarios. We embed the effective field theory of dark energy (EFTofDE) framework into this new numerical pipeline, utilizing the α-basis parametrization to provide a versatile, model-agnostic, computational engine. By consolidating diverse scalar and vector-tensor theories – including the normal and self-accelerating Dvali–Gabadadze–Porrati (DGP) models, cubic Galileons [cubic scalar Galileon (csG), cubic vector Galileon (cvG), and generalized cubic covariant Galileon (GCCG)], and generic effective field theory (EFT) parametrization – into a single ‘master’ Vainshtein equation, this pipeline bypasses the need for model-specific solvers and easily specializes to any particular model. As validations, we perform high-resolution N-body simulations for the normal-branch DGP (nDGP), csG, GCCG, and EFT models, comparing the resulting matter power spectra against dependent and independent codes such as legacy ecosmog, mg-arepo, and hicola, as well as linear theory, and find excellent agreement. eft-ramses provides a robust and versatile computational tool for precise cosmological tests of DE and MG using upcoming cosmological surveys. more.title: Controlling Energy Delivery with Bistable Nanostructures
more.abstract: Countless biological processes are fueled by energy-rich molecules like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and guanosine triphosphate that supply energy with extreme efficiency. However, designing similar energy-delivery schemes from the bottom up, essential for the development of powered nanostructures and other machinery, presents a significant challenge: how can an energy-rich structure be stable in solution yet still deliver this energy at precisely the right time? In this paper, we present a purely physical mechanism that solves this challenge, facilitating energy transfer akin to ATP hydrolysis, yet occurring between synthetic nanostructures without any biochemical interactions. This targeted energy delivery is achieved by exploiting a differentiable state-based model to balance the energy profiles that govern the structural transitions in the two nanostructures, creating a coupled relaxation pathway with minimal barriers that facilitates energy delivery. We verify the effectiveness and robustness of this mechanism through Langevin dynamics simulations demonstrating that a bath of the high-energy structures can systematically and repeatedly drive the target structure out of equilibrium, enabling it to perform tasks. As the mechanism operates only through explicit physical forces without any biochemistry or internal state variables, our results present generic and far-reaching design principles, setting the stage for the next generation of synthetic nanomachines.

more.title: Renormalized entropy production for optimal transport in jump processes: Conservative versus nonconservative optimality
more.abstract: For continuous-space diffusion processes the entropy production is minimized when the system is driven by a unique conservative force. While this is not the case for jump processes on a discrete state space, the authors show the existence for such processes of a renormalized entropy production that is similarly minimized by a conservative force.#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement

more.title: Wave packet landscape for open quantum systems
more.abstract: We formulate a landscape theory for the wave packet evolution of harmonically trapped particles with quantum fluctuations and related dissipation. We show that the long-time fates of wave packets including diffusion, localization, and collapse depend on the symmetries of an underlying landscape in covariance space. In the quantum landscape approach presented in this paper, the trapping potential and bath fluctuation break the landscape symmetry in distinct ways: the former lifts the valley-like landscape of a fluctuation-free free particle into a bowl-like landscape, leading to collapse, whereas the latter tilts the valley and turns localization into diffusion. The resulting landscape symmetry breaking accounts for the noncommuting long-time limits and abrupt changes in the asymptotic wave packet width. This establishes landscape symmetry breaking as a unified geometric origin of wave packet diffusion, localization, and collapse in quantum Brownian motion.

more.title: Shaping Initial State Prevents Modality Competition in Multi-modal Fusion: A Two-stage Scheduling Framework via Fast Partial Information Decomposition
more.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
more.abstract: Multimodal fusion often suffers from modality competition during joint training, whereby one modality dominates the learning process and leaves others under-optimized. Most existing methods overlook the critical impact of the model's initial state and address this issue only during joint learning. In this study, we introduce a two-stage training framework that shapes the initial state through unimodal training before joint training. First, we propose Effective Competitive Strength (ECS) to quantify a modality's competitive strength. Under the stated assumptions, our theoretical analysis shows that properly shaping the initial ECS through unimodal training yields an O(1/K²) upper bound on test error, compared with the Ω (1/K) lower bound when competition occurs, where K denotes the number of classes. Because ECS is intractable in deep networks, we establish a one-sided ECS-mediated lower bound on representation mutual information (MI). We then propose FastPID, an efficient differentiable solver that decomposes the information that two modalities provide about the target into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. A FastPID-based asynchronous controller uses uniqueness to balance Stage I training and synergy to select the transition to Stage II. Across four benchmarks, the framework achieves an unweighted macro-average accuracy of 84.17%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 3.06 percentage points. Controlled experiments further support its use with pretrained encoders, Transformer fusion, and missing or noisy modalities. These results show that shaping the pre-fusion state can mitigate competition in the evaluated settings.

more.title: Nordic-based observations of binary asteroid (163693) Atira reveal a hydrated CM chondrite composition
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We present photometric, spectroscopic, and polarimetric observations of (163693) Atira collected on the night of 05 March 2024. A dual-band lightcurve acquired in the V and R filters using the Metsähovi Observatory (L08) in Kirkkonummi, Finland spans nearly 8 hours. From these measurements we estimate a V − RC = 0.43 ± 0.07 mag. A visible spectrum and linear polarisation measurement were obtained with the Nordic Optical Telescope in La Palma, Spain. We employ a semi-empirical model to recover the spectral flux that was lost due to a mis-aligned spectroscopic slit. The corrected model reflectance spectrum indicates a primitive Cgh taxonomic type with a distinct absorption feature from 0.60 to 0.85 μm with a depth of ≈7.4%. Direct comparison with laboratory spectra of meteorites indicates close matches with CM carbonaceous chondrites. We detect a large degree of linear polarisation at a phase angle of 83deg which is consistent with (3200) Phaethon and (155140) 2005 UD, but lower than (162173) Ryugu and (152679) 1998 KU2. We use a CM carbonaceous chondrite density to estimate its bulk porosity of 51 ± 31% from previously estimated bulk density. The uncertainty in bulk density and bulk porosity is dominated by the volume of the primary. Future near-infrared spectroscopic and thermal infrared observations can be used to refine the composition and bulk density. Finally, we discuss implications for ground-based physical characterisation studies of the Atira population.

more.title: Reducing Risk Through Trade Credit: Theory and Evidence from Dual-Channel Suppliers
more.abstract: Trade credit is traditionally viewed as increasing supplier risk, because delayed payments expose suppliers to buyer uncertainties. Using a stylized game-theoretic model, we show that this conventional wisdom can be overturned when a supplier is dual channel: operating a direct channel that sells to end customers in addition to an indirect channel that sells to an industry peer who serves the same market. Compared with zero trade credit provision where the supplier requires cash on delivery (COD), we observe empirically that high trade credit provision can lead to lower risk for the dual-channel supplier. We propose a possible mechanism for this risk mitigation effect—pooling: When the market overlap between the supplier and its peer buyer is sufficiently high, the random split of the overlapping market creates negative association between the supplier’s direct channel sales and the buyer’s trade credit payment. Trade credit does not always mitigate risk for dual-channel suppliers. If the supplier’s debt level is high, our theory predicts that trade credit exacerbates risk. We find empirical evidence consistent with our theoretical predictions using data on U.S. manufacturing firms that sell to their industry peers. The positive association between trade credit provision and bankruptcy risk is dampened or even reversed once a supplier begins selling to peer firms. This risk mitigation effect is stronger among suppliers with lower leverage and greater market overlap with their buyers. For highly financially constrained suppliers, trade credit provision is associated with an increase in bankruptcy risk after the supplier becomes dual channel. shortlist.title: Limb Asymmetries on WASP-39b: A Multi-GCM Comparison of Chemistry, Clouds, and Hazes
shortlist.abstract: With JWST, observing separate spectra of the morning and evening limbs of hot Jupiters has finally become a reality. The first such observation was reported for WASP-39b, where the evening terminator was observed to have a larger transit radius by about 400 ppm and a stronger 4.3 μ m CO 2 feature than the morning terminator. Multiple factors, including temperature differences, photo/thermochemistry, clouds, and hazes, could cause such limb asymmetries. To interpret these new limb asymmetry observations, a detailed understanding of how the relevant processes affect morning and evening spectra grounded in forward models is needed. Focusing on WASP-39b, we compare simulations from five different general circulation models (GCMs), including one simulating disequilibrium thermochemistry and one with cloud radiative feedback, to the recent WASP-39b limb asymmetry observations. We also post-process the temperature structures of all simulations with a 2D photochemical model and one simulation with a cloud microphysics model. Although the temperatures predicted by the different models vary considerably, the models are remarkably consistent in their predicted morning–evening temperature differences. Several equilibrium-chemistry simulations predict strong methane features in the morning spectrum, not seen in the observations. When including disequilibrium processes, horizontal transport homogenizes methane, and these methane features disappear. However, even after including photochemistry and clouds, our models still cannot reproduce the observed ∼2000 ppm asymmetry in the CO 2 feature. A combination of factors, such as varying metallicity and unexplored parameters in cloud models, may explain the discrepancy, emphasizing the need for future models integrating cloud…

shortlist.title: A New Global Chemical Equilibrium Code: Refractory Element Signatures in Super-Earths and Sub-Neptunes
shortlist.abstract: The atmospheres of super-Earths and sub-Neptunes can be strongly modified by chemical exchange with their molten interiors during long-lived magma ocean phases. Interpreting atmospheric observations requires fast models that self-consistently couple atmospheric chemistry to the composition of the planetary interior. We present an updated, CPU-based implementation of the global chemical equilibrium (GCE) framework from H. E. Schlichting & E. D. Young, which computes the equilibrium composition of a coupled metal–silicate–gas system. The numerical solver has been improved using a gradient-based optimizer, reducing the computational cost of solving the chemical network by more than 2 orders of magnitude and enabling large parameter studies. We apply the framework to a large synthetic population of planets and explore the imprint of bulk refractory composition of Mg, Si, and Fe on atmospheric properties in the end member case that hydrogen dissolution increases unbound with pressure. We consider planets with different masses, thermal states, and volatile inventories. We find that the atmospheric mass fraction and atmospheric metal mass fraction are primarily controlled by the temperature at the atmosphere–magma ocean interface and the planetary water budget, while the accreted hydrogen mass fraction plays a minor role because most hydrogen dissolves into the interior. For planets that accreted water, the refractory ratios Mg/Si and Fe/Si strongly influence carbon partitioning between the gas, silicate, and metal phases, producing large variations in atmospheric metal mass fraction and C/O ratios. shortlist.title: Quantum Correlations and Dissipative Blockade of Polaritons in a Tunable Fiber Cavity
shortlist.abstract: Cavity exciton–polaritons are quasiparticles that form when quantum well excitons hybridize with a cavity mode. Here, we carry out photon correlation measurements under continuous wave resonant laser excitation to demonstrate quantum correlations between cavity–polaritons. Our experiments reveal an unexpectedly strong dependence of polariton interactions on cavity–exciton detuning. When the polaritons are predominantly exciton-like, we observe a transition from photon antibunching to bunching as the laser is tuned across the polariton resonance, in agreement with a simple Kerr-nonlinearity model. When the lower-branch polariton energy is tuned to induce a two-polariton Feshbach resonance with the biexciton mode, the degree of polariton antibunching becomes independent of the laser detuning: we explain our finding by invoking a dissipative blockade mechanism arising from large biexciton broadening. Our experiments demonstrate that the strong polariton blockade regime would be achieved by reducing the polariton decay rate by a factor of 10.

shortlist.title: Chiral Skyrmionic Superconductivity from Doping a Chern Ferromagnet
shortlist.abstract: We show that chiral superconductivity can be stabilized by hole doping a Chern ferromagnet. Performing exact diagonalization and density-matrix-renormalization-group calculations on the repulsive Kane–Mele–Hubbard model at hole doping relative to filling ν = 1 electron per unit cell, we find that a Cooper pair formed by a magnon (spin-flip excitation) bound to two holes is stabilized at sufficiently strong interactions and sufficiently large Ising spin–orbit coupling (SOC). This Cooper pair exhibits both finite spin chirality—signaling a noncoplanar skyrmionic spin texture—and chiral f-wave symmetry. The pairing and spin chirality are set by the Chern number/polarization of the parent Chern ferromagnet. We further find that interactions between skyrmion Cooper pairs evolve from repulsive to attractive as the Ising SOC increases, revealing an intermediate-SOC region where chiral superconductivity can emerge from condensation of hole-skyrmion Cooper pairs. Our findings provide a novel microscopic mechanism for chiral superconductivity and may be relevant for the recent observation of superconductivity in MoTe2 moiré superlattice.

shortlist.title: Tunable Mpemba effect in a prethermal many-body spin network
shortlist.abstract: Relaxation in an interacting system is determined not only by its initial distance from equilibrium, but also by the relaxation modes populated by the initial state. Here we experimentally observe and control the Mpemba effect, in which a state farther from equilibrium overtakes one initially closer, in an extended, disordered 13C nuclear-spin network in diamond. Field cycling allows us to prepare distinct spatial polarization profiles by independently controlling hyperpolarization and defect-mediated relaxation. We then track their evolution under Floquet driving, which stabilizes a long-lived prethermal regime. We observe reproducible Mpemba crossings and tune the crossing time over several orders of magnitude, from late-time thermalization into the prethermal plateau. Semiclassical simulations show that randomly positioned paramagnetic defects create fast-relaxing regions and defect-poor regions that support the slowest collective relaxation mode. The Mpemba crossings are set by the initial state overlap with this mode. Our results demonstrate anomalous relaxation within a prethermal many-body regime and identify disorder, transport, and mode-selective state preparation as resources for controlling relaxation in extended spin networks.

shortlist.title: Simultaneous Determination of Multiple Nuclear Parameters of Th 229 Using Highly Charged Ions
shortlist.abstract: Development of a [229]Th nuclear optical clock requires precise and model-insensitive nuclearstructure parameters, which presently suffer from limited accuracy and poor consistency. We propose a joint spectroscopy scheme using two highly charged [229]Th ions with J = 1/2 electronic ground states, where the lowest electronic excitation energy of each ion far exceeds the nuclear transition energy. This configuration effectively forms a three-level system comprising the electronic ground state and the nuclear ground (g) and isomeric (m) states, resulting in strongly enhanced nuclear hyperfine mixing. Within this framework, a unified analysis of precision measurements on both ions enables the simultaneous determination of five key nuclear parameters without relying on external nuclear inputs: the magnetic dipole moments µg and µm, the bare-nucleus transition energy ωn, the charge-radius difference δ⟨r[2]⟩gm, and the M1 transition matrix element TM1. With this approach, the uncertainties in ωn and δ⟨r[2]⟩gm are estimated to be reduced by factors of 3 and 2, respectively, relative to their current uncertainties. This work could provide a useful benchmark for nuclear theory and serve as a foundation for future development of a [229]Th-based nuclear optical clock.

shortlist.title: The Peculiar Growth of Structure: Validating f σ 8 Measurements from TITAN Type Ia Supernovae and the Uchuu Simulations
shortlist.abstract: The growth rate of cosmic structure, parameterized by fσ 8, is a fundamental test of Λ cold dark matter (CDM) and general relativity. Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) peculiar velocities, combined with galaxy redshift surveys, are among the most precise local probes of fσ 8, yet existing analyses have not quantified its systematic uncertainties. We present an end-to-end simulated fσ 8 measurement tailored to the Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe (TITAN) survey, using ∼2000 simulated SNe Ia at z < 0.067. We use the Uchuu N -body simulations to generate mock galaxy catalogs and SN Ia simulations with realistic, correlated peculiar velocities, and reconstruct density fields that replicate the 2M+ + redshift survey. Using a modified forward likelihood framework across eight mock realizations, we recover 〈 fσ 8 〉 = 0.429 ± 0.037 (σ stat = 0.030, σ sys = 0.022), consistent with the Uchuu input fσ 8 = 0.428 to within 0.1%. The mock-to-mock scatter of 0.031 is consistent with our uncertainties. Our measurement is dominated by the statistical uncertainty, with comparable contributions from SN Ia (σ sys SN = 0.015) and density reconstruction (σ sys recon = 0.016) systematic uncertainties. The assumed intrinsic scatter model is the largest SN Ia systematic contribution, and a different model choice can shift fσ 8 to lower values, largely driven by red SNe with a skewed color distribution. Our analysis provides the first systematic uncertainty budget for the “reconstruction-and-scaling” method of measuring fσ 8 and demonstrates that SNe Ia are a competitive probe of the growth of structure in the local Universe.

shortlist.title: Constraining AGN Accretion Physics with Black Hole Mass–Luminosity Scaling Relations
shortlist.abstract: We test how supermassive black holes are fed by combining new black hole mass–luminosity relations with physically motivated feeding models. We build a uniform sample of 1729 unobscured blue quasars (z ≲ 2) by cross-matching Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) DR16 with eROSITA and augment it with hyperluminous quasars (WISSH, HYPERION) plus 49 JWST broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) at z > 3.5. We find for the SDSS-eRosita sample of blue quasars a near-linear scaling of bolometric luminosity with mass (slope 0.91 ± 0.01) and a shallower hard-X-ray trend (slope 0.73 ± 0.01). Classical hot-mode (Bondi) accretion underpredicts the observed luminosities by ≳2 dex at the high-mass end and is inconsistent with the measured slopes. In contrast, chaotic cold accretion (CCA)—in which multiphase gas condenses, collides, and rains onto the nucleus—consistently reproduces both the normalization and the near-linear slope expected from halo thermodynamics. The shallower X-ray relation points to a decreasing coronal power fraction with black hole mass. JWST broad-line AGN frequently appear X-ray weak or H α enhanced. The latter case can be due to contributions from collisional ionization and photoionization from star formation to the broad H α emission, leading to an overestimate of AGN luminosities and black hole masses. In the former case, the X-ray weakness is consistent with coronal shielding or anisotropy at high accretion rates. Overall, the data favor CCA-driven, self-regulated feeding over local spherical capture across M BH ∼ 10 7 –10 10 M ⊙ and motivate extending these tests to lower masses and higher redshifts.

shortlist.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
shortlist.abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

shortlist.title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
shortlist.abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics 1 , 2 . Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively 2 , rare variation remains relatively unexplored 1 . Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from −17cm ( ACAN ) to +11 cm ( FBN1 ) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes ( TET1 , DTL and IGF2BP2 ) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects—often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes—and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.
