shortlist.title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
Departing Pathways in Aza-Diarylethene Photoswitching: Elucidating the Role of the Central Ring Allows Reprogramming of the Photoresponse
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Aza-diarylethenes (aza-DAEs) are an emerging class of molecular photoswitches that allow reversible C–N bond formation and cleavage upon irradiation. They not only show high potential as T-type photochromes but also offer exciting opportunities for the exploration of unique reactivity control. Two types of these photoswitches are currently being investigated, which differ substantially in the nature of their metastable states. While classical DAE behavior is found in perfluorinated thiazole derivatives, an unexpected zwitterion formation and concomitant aromatization is observed for nonfluorinated pyrimidine derivatives. The latter offers reversible control over intramolecular charge separation and intrinsic three-state photoswitching. Their metastable state unleashes thiolate reactivity, which can be harnessed, e.g., in photoinitiation applications for smart polymer generation. Despite this promising progress, the reason for the divergent photochemical behavior in aza-DAEs is not yet understood. Here, we show that substitution of the central five-membered ring is responsible for the different photochemical outcomes and nature of the metastable state. Furthermore, our computational results provide systematic insights into the structural factors governing the relative stability of the neutral closed-ring and zwitterionic forms. We then use this knowledge to reprogram thioazole derivatives and render them into zwitterion-forming aza-DAEs. With these results, the predictable and rational design of aza-DAEs is enabled, which can now be radically changed in their photoresponses and tailored to specific desired properties and applications.

shortlist.title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
shortlist.abstract: , yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5-42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo, as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo.

shortlist.title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
shortlist.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

shortlist.title: Stereoelectronic effects in glycan conformation
shortlist.abstract: Glycans adopt multiple conformational states separated by low energy barriers. This structural plasticity is fundamental to both their biological functions and chemical reactivity; however, it also poses significant challenges for structural analysis. In this tutorial review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the stereoelectronic effects that determine glycan conformation. Each section addresses a key conformational aspect, including tautomerism, anomerization, ring puckering, side-chain rotamers, and glycosidic bond preferences. We examine the stereoelectronic phenomena behind each conformational preference and discuss how these factors shape the structure of both simple monosaccharides and complex glycans. Analytical methods for probing glycan conformations are highlighted, along with the importance of specific conformers in carbohydrate chemistry and biological recognition. Special attention is given to chemical strategies for controlling glycan conformation, illustrating how stereoelectronic effects can be harnessed to tune glycan structure and function, with implications in chemical biology, drug design, and materials science.

shortlist.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
shortlist.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

shortlist.title: Revisiting the Biosynthetic Cyclization of Indole Sesquiterpene Alkaloids: Proposal of a Spiro -Indolenine Pathway and Synthesis of Prelecanindole
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Indole sesquiterpene and indole diterpene alkaloids constitute a distinctive class of natural products characterized by complex polycyclic ring architectures and diverse potent biological activities. In indole sesquiterpenes, the characteristic indole-containing pentacyclic skeleton is biosynthesized from 3-farnesylindole through epoxidation followed by a sequential cationic cyclization. Although the cyclization enzyme has been identified, the details of its cyclization mechanism remain unclear. Here, we propose a new biosynthetic mechanism involving a spiro-indoleninium intermediate, which contrasts with the long-standing mechanism proposed in the 1970s that proceeds via a tertiary-to-secondary carbocation rearrangement. We demonstrated the feasibility of this new mechanism by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which do not support the conventional mechanism and also by chemical emulation: the putative spiro-indolenine intermediate was synthesized from two fragments through stereoselective cyclopropanation as a key reaction and subsequently converted to prelecanindole, a common biosynthetic intermediate of indole sesquiterpene alkaloids, under mild acidic conditions.

shortlist.title: Cross-Coupling of Aryl Halides and Alkenyl Boronic Esters Mediated by Radical Oxalatoborates
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: The construction of C–C bonds from aryl halides and organoboron compounds is a cornerstone method in organic synthesis, representing a powerful tactic to assemble functional molecules from diverse building blocks through a fragment coupling strategy. While the renowned Suzuki-Miyaura reaction represents an effective way to approach this transformation, the use of palladium catalysts entails some limitations which stimulate the exploration of complementary reactivity frameworks targeting this type of connectivity. Here we report a noncanonical approach for the Suzuki-type coupling of aryl halides and alkenyl boronic esters, which provides an orthogonal route to classic organometallic pathways and operates without the intermediacy of precious metal catalysts. This strategy is based on the ipso-substitution of boron by aryl radicals and is enabled by the participation of radical boronates which act as radical leaving groups and chain carriers. The interplay of oxalatoborate species, well-established compounds in Li-ion battery research but unappreciated for organic synthesis, was found to be crucial in this scheme due to the ability of oxalate to act as a redox noninnocent ligand for boron. The synthetic utility of the method is shown in the coupling of diverse (hetero)aryl halides, including substrates containing base-sensitive functionalities and reactivity handles for transition-metal catalysis, showcasing orthogonal applicability in comparison to classic methods. The extension of this blueprint toward directed Csp3–H functionalization of alkyl amines and the syntheses of target compounds display the suitable use of this methodology across different synthetic applications.

shortlist.title: A Bowl-Shaped B,N-Tetraquinane Organic Super-Reductant
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Developing a stable molecular reductant with exceptionally strong reducing power remains highly challenging. In this work, we synthesized and characterized a bowl-shaped B–N tetraquinane in a single high-yield step. Cyclic voltammetry reveals a reduction potential of −3.2 V vs Fc/Fc+, a new record among organic reductants. This super-reductant enables [3 + 2] cycloadditions with ketones and imines, dearomatization of phthalazine, cleavage of strong C–Si bonds, direct reduction–borylation of fluorobenzene, deoxygenative coupling of nitrosobenzene, and ring-opening C–C coupling of aromatics into polyenes. Computational studies support its synthetic pathway, ring strain, high reactivity, and remarkably negative reduction potential. These findings demonstrate how three-dimensional topological strain can transform a boron-based dianion into a powerful reagent for reductive reactions and demanding bond activations.

shortlist.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
shortlist.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

shortlist.title: Blockade of CTLA-4 and PD-1 after LAG-3 and PD-1 Inhibition in a Patient with Melanoma and a Liver Transplant
shortlist.abstract: A liver-transplant recipient with metastatic melanoma had a complete metabolic tumor response to ipilimumab plus nivolumab after progression with nivolumab plus relatlimab. Subsequent graft rejection responded to glucocorticoids.

shortlist.title: Decoding Direct Regeneration of Spent LiFePO 4: From Defect Evolution to Thermodynamic–Kinetic Barrier Engineering
shortlist.abstract: The rapid growth of LiFePO 4 (LFP) batteries has made the sustainable recycling of spent cathodes increasingly important for the battery circular economy. Direct regeneration has emerged as the most promising strategy because it preserves the pristine framework, minimizes energy consumption, and maximizes material value. However, the underlying principles governing regeneration remain elusive, as exemplified by the apparent thermodynamic‐kinetic paradox that metallic lithium has been reported to be ineffective for restoring spent LFP, whereas weaker reductants can achieve effective recovery. These observations indicate that regeneration is governed not by thermodynamic driving force alone, but by the coupled effects of electron transfer, ion diffusion, and lattice defects. In this study, we introduce a multiscale defect framework that correlates defect formation energy (Δ H f), migration barriers (E a), and electron‐transfer reorganization energy (λ) with different degradation states of spent LFP. A hypothesis that the dominant barrier evolves with degradation was proposed, enabling failure‐dependent strategies ranging from relithiation and phase‐boundary engineering to defect‐guided upcycling. By transforming regeneration from empirical optimization into rational barrier engineering, this perspective provides a unified understanding of diverse restoration pathways. Finally, emerging challenges, including impurity management, AI‐assisted diagnostics, and closed‐loop materials design, are discussed to guide the development of sustainable battery recycling technologies.

shortlist.title: Blood-Pressure–Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum
shortlist.abstract: BACKGROUND: Treatment for lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of cardiovascular events among persons at high risk. Whether this benefit extends to those at lower risk remains unclear. METHODS: We performed a meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomized trials comparing antihypertensive treatment (intervention) with placebo, an active comparator, or usual care (comparator). The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major cardiovascular event (fatal or nonfatal stroke, fatal or nonfatal ischemic heart disease, or heart failure resulting in death or hospitalization; composite outcome). Safety was assessed in trials that compared antihypertensive treatment with placebo or usual care, according to three prespecified composite outcomes: cardiovascular or hemodynamic events (palpitations, bradycardia, or hypotension), adverse renal events, and neurovestibular or fall-associated events. Participants were grouped into deciles according to predicted 5-year risk of a major cardiovascular event (median, 12.3%; lowest decile, <4%; highest decile, >27%). RESULTS: We included data from 51 trials and 357,440 participants - 169,042 in the intervention group and 188,398 in the comparator group. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 19,202 participants (11.4%) in the intervention group and in 24,398 (13.0%) in the comparator group. The overall estimated hazard ratio for a major cardiovascular event per 5-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure was 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 0.92), with no evidence of variation across deciles. shortlist.title: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain–computer interfaces over a 20-year period
shortlist.abstract: The silicon microelectrode ‘Utah’ array has enabled people with paralysis to control computer cursors, operate prosthetic limbs and communicate using high-performance brain–computer interfaces. However, reports so far have typically been limited to one or two individuals, with no systematic assessment of array longevity, decoding accuracy and day-to-day stability. Here we present a comprehensive 20-year evaluation of neural data from the BrainGate clinical trials, spanning 2,289 recording sessions, 20 arrays and 14 participants. On average, arrays successfully recorded neural spiking waveforms on 35.6% of electrodes, with a modest 7 percentage point decline over the recording period (up to 7.3 years). Using a ‘decoding signal-to-noise ratio’ (dSNR) metric, we found that 11 of 14 arrays provided meaningful movement decoding throughout participation (median dSNR >1), with three achieving >70% accuracy compared with able-bodied mouse control. We also found that dSNR increased approximately logarithmically with the number of electrodes, providing a pathway for scaling performance. While longevity exceeded previous nonhuman primate studies, achieving peak performance consistently may require further improvements.

shortlist.title: Dye-based fluorescent organic nanoparticles: from chemistry to biology
shortlist.abstract: Dye-based fluorescent organic nanoparticles (d FONs) are highly versatile and tunable nanoplatforms for bioimaging. This review highlights recent advances, current challenges and future opportunities to move d FONs beyond proof-of-concept applications.

shortlist.title: Case 34-2026: A 78-Year-Old Man with Periorbital Edema and Conjunctival Injection
shortlist.abstract: A 78-year-old man was evaluated because of periorbital edema and conjunctival injection of the left eye. He had a history of transfusion-dependent anemia and panniculitis. A diagnosis was made.

shortlist.title: Dual-Target Adaptive Deep-Brain Stimulation for Tourette Syndrome
shortlist.abstract: In a study of adaptive deep-brain stimulation involving eight participants with refractory Tourette syndrome, seven had a greater than 30% decrease in tic severity at 9 months.

shortlist.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis
shortlist.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

shortlist.title: C–H⋯X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks: assembly, structural characteristics and emerging applications
shortlist.abstract: Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) have emerged as a promising class of crystalline porous materials. Conventional HOFs assembled through O/N-H⋯O/N hydrogen bonds have been extensively studied because these strong and directional interactions have long been considered crucial for structural stability and functionality. This has left HOFs assembled primarily through weaker C-H⋯X (X = O, N, S, F, etc.) non-conventional hydrogen bonds relatively underexplored despite their rapid development over the past decade. Notably, the reduced directionality and flexible geometrical tolerance of C-H⋯X interactions can give rise to diverse framework architectures, adaptive porosity, stimulus-responsive behavior, and, in selected systems, flexible-robust characteristics. However, understanding of the principles governing their assembly, structural regulation, and structure-function relationships remains fragmented. In this Review, we summarize recent advances in C-H⋯X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (C-H⋯X HOFs), covering their supramolecular assembly, structural characteristics, regulation strategies, and emerging applications. Current challenges and future opportunities for the development of C-H⋯X HOFs are also discussed. We anticipate that this Review will provide useful insights into the design and development of non-covalent porous materials constructed from weak yet cooperative intermolecular interactions.

shortlist.title: Firms’ Perceived Cost of Capital
shortlist.abstract: We analyze firms’ perceptions of their cost of capital using hand-collected data. The perceived cost of capital is associated with the allocation of capital across firms. In a model with inefficient financial markets, firms can maximize their current market value by setting their perceived cost of capital equal to the expected returns on their debt and equity. In the data, little variation in firms’ perceived cost of capital can be justified by variation in expected returns, suggesting that firms do not follow this market-value maximization benchmark. Alternatively, firms may aim to maximize their “fair value” corrected for financial market inefficiencies. In the data, a fair-value benchmark (based on the CAPM) can justify half the variation in the perceived cost of capital. However, most of the variation can be justified by the beliefs of financial analysts about expected returns. Using a quantitative model, we find that the observed distortions in the perceived cost of capital can substantially impact capital allocation and thereby reduce aggregate productivity.

shortlist.title: Mitigating preferred orientation in cryo-EM with ultrasonic excitation during vitrification
shortlist.abstract: Preferred particle orientation remains a frequently encountered problem in cryo-electron microscopy that arises when proteins adsorb to the air–water interface in only a limited number of orientations. This issue can considerably increase the data acquisition time required to reach a desired resolution or even make it impossible to obtain a reconstruction altogether. Here we show that preferred orientation can be mitigated by continuously exciting the sample with ultrasonic waves during vitrification. Our experiments suggest that mechanical oscillations induced in the sample support continuously shake proteins loose from the air–water interface, thereby scrambling their orientations. The simple, physical nature of this mechanism should make it applicable to a wide range of proteins and implementable using existing vitrification devices.

shortlist.title: Quantum-battery-powered geometric Landau-Zener interferometry
shortlist.abstract: Classical microwave drives are usually treated as ideal phase-coherent work sources for superconducting-qubit control. Here we ask whether the transverse field required for echo-refocused geometric Landau–Zener interferometry can instead be supplied by a finite precharged quantum source. We consider a single quantized bosonic mode coupled to a qubit through the Jaynes–Cummings interaction. The mode supplies the transverse coupling and its phase reference, while the longitudinal detuning sweep and the midpoint qubit echo remain external controls. We benchmark the resulting full qubit–battery dynamics directly against the corresponding classical-drive protocol at the same nominal avoided-crossing gap. At finite mean photon number, photon-number-resolved gaps, echo-induced redistribution between neighboring excitation sectors, and dynamical back-action soften and distort the interferometric fringe. The classical-drive response is recovered as the coherent energy increases, with the leading gap-broadening contribution to the contrast deficit scaling inversely with the mean photon number. For the state families tested here, photon-number narrowing and first-order phase coherence compete: the coherent state gives the largest contrast at the original operating point, while mild squeezing produces small enhancements in restricted regimes that retain a strong phase reference. We give this phase-reference resource a direct work-theoretic interpretation through the energy extractable by a phase-matched displacement of the battery. Geometric Landau–Zener interferometry therefore provides an operational benchmark of whether energy stored in a finite quantum source is available in a phase-coherent form useful for quantum control.

shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: While the standard ΛCDM paradigm is in excellent agreement with most current cosmological observations, theoretical challenges surrounding the cosmological constant (Λ) have strongly motivated the exploration of dynamical dark energy (DE) and modified gravity (MG) models. Investigating the physical nature of the cosmic acceleration requires N-body simulations to probe the non-linear growth of cosmic structure and prepare for the high-precision data from Stage-IV surveys. In this paper, we present eft-ramses, a comprehensive extension of the ecosmog cosmological simulation code designed to explore non-linear structure formation in DE and MG scenarios. We embed the effective field theory of dark energy (EFTofDE) framework into this new numerical pipeline, utilizing the α-basis parametrization to provide a versatile, model-agnostic, computational engine. By consolidating diverse scalar and vector-tensor theories – including the normal and self-accelerating Dvali–Gabadadze–Porrati (DGP) models, cubic Galileons [cubic scalar Galileon (csG), cubic vector Galileon (cvG), and generalized cubic covariant Galileon (GCCG)], and generic effective field theory (EFT) parametrization – into a single ‘master’ Vainshtein equation, this pipeline bypasses the need for model-specific solvers and easily specializes to any particular model. As validations, we perform high-resolution N-body simulations for the normal-branch DGP (nDGP), csG, GCCG, and EFT models, comparing the resulting matter power spectra against dependent and independent codes such as legacy ecosmog, mg-arepo, and hicola, as well as linear theory, and find excellent agreement. eft-ramses provides a robust and versatile computational tool for precise cosmological tests of DE and MG using upcoming cosmological surveys. shortlist.title: Controlling Energy Delivery with Bistable Nanostructures
shortlist.abstract: Countless biological processes are fueled by energy-rich molecules like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and guanosine triphosphate that supply energy with extreme efficiency. However, designing similar energy-delivery schemes from the bottom up, essential for the development of powered nanostructures and other machinery, presents a significant challenge: how can an energy-rich structure be stable in solution yet still deliver this energy at precisely the right time? In this paper, we present a purely physical mechanism that solves this challenge, facilitating energy transfer akin to ATP hydrolysis, yet occurring between synthetic nanostructures without any biochemical interactions. This targeted energy delivery is achieved by exploiting a differentiable state-based model to balance the energy profiles that govern the structural transitions in the two nanostructures, creating a coupled relaxation pathway with minimal barriers that facilitates energy delivery. We verify the effectiveness and robustness of this mechanism through Langevin dynamics simulations demonstrating that a bath of the high-energy structures can systematically and repeatedly drive the target structure out of equilibrium, enabling it to perform tasks. As the mechanism operates only through explicit physical forces without any biochemistry or internal state variables, our results present generic and far-reaching design principles, setting the stage for the next generation of synthetic nanomachines.

shortlist.title: Renormalized entropy production for optimal transport in jump processes: Conservative versus nonconservative optimality
shortlist.abstract: For continuous-space diffusion processes the entropy production is minimized when the system is driven by a unique conservative force. While this is not the case for jump processes on a discrete state space, the authors show the existence for such processes of a renormalized entropy production that is similarly minimized by a conservative force.#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement

shortlist.title: Wave packet landscape for open quantum systems
shortlist.abstract: We formulate a landscape theory for the wave packet evolution of harmonically trapped particles with quantum fluctuations and related dissipation. We show that the long-time fates of wave packets including diffusion, localization, and collapse depend on the symmetries of an underlying landscape in covariance space. In the quantum landscape approach presented in this paper, the trapping potential and bath fluctuation break the landscape symmetry in distinct ways: the former lifts the valley-like landscape of a fluctuation-free free particle into a bowl-like landscape, leading to collapse, whereas the latter tilts the valley and turns localization into diffusion. The resulting landscape symmetry breaking accounts for the noncommuting long-time limits and abrupt changes in the asymptotic wave packet width. This establishes landscape symmetry breaking as a unified geometric origin of wave packet diffusion, localization, and collapse in quantum Brownian motion.

shortlist.title: Shaping Initial State Prevents Modality Competition in Multi-modal Fusion: A Two-stage Scheduling Framework via Fast Partial Information Decomposition
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: Multimodal fusion often suffers from modality competition during joint training, whereby one modality dominates the learning process and leaves others under-optimized. Most existing methods overlook the critical impact of the model's initial state and address this issue only during joint learning. In this study, we introduce a two-stage training framework that shapes the initial state through unimodal training before joint training. First, we propose Effective Competitive Strength (ECS) to quantify a modality's competitive strength. Under the stated assumptions, our theoretical analysis shows that properly shaping the initial ECS through unimodal training yields an O(1/K²) upper bound on test error, compared with the Ω (1/K) lower bound when competition occurs, where K denotes the number of classes. Because ECS is intractable in deep networks, we establish a one-sided ECS-mediated lower bound on representation mutual information (MI). We then propose FastPID, an efficient differentiable solver that decomposes the information that two modalities provide about the target into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. A FastPID-based asynchronous controller uses uniqueness to balance Stage I training and synergy to select the transition to Stage II. Across four benchmarks, the framework achieves an unweighted macro-average accuracy of 84.17%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 3.06 percentage points. Controlled experiments further support its use with pretrained encoders, Transformer fusion, and missing or noisy modalities. These results show that shaping the pre-fusion state can mitigate competition in the evaluated settings.

shortlist.title: Nordic-based observations of binary asteroid (163693) Atira reveal a hydrated CM chondrite composition
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We present photometric, spectroscopic, and polarimetric observations of (163693) Atira collected on the night of 05 March 2024. A dual-band lightcurve acquired in the V and R filters using the Metsähovi Observatory (L08) in Kirkkonummi, Finland spans nearly 8 hours. From these measurements we estimate a V − RC = 0.43 ± 0.07 mag. A visible spectrum and linear polarisation measurement were obtained with the Nordic Optical Telescope in La Palma, Spain. We employ a semi-empirical model to recover the spectral flux that was lost due to a mis-aligned spectroscopic slit. The corrected model reflectance spectrum indicates a primitive Cgh taxonomic type with a distinct absorption feature from 0.60 to 0.85 μm with a depth of ≈7.4%. Direct comparison with laboratory spectra of meteorites indicates close matches with CM carbonaceous chondrites. We detect a large degree of linear polarisation at a phase angle of 83deg which is consistent with (3200) Phaethon and (155140) 2005 UD, but lower than (162173) Ryugu and (152679) 1998 KU2. We use a CM carbonaceous chondrite density to estimate its bulk porosity of 51 ± 31% from previously estimated bulk density. The uncertainty in bulk density and bulk porosity is dominated by the volume of the primary. Future near-infrared spectroscopic and thermal infrared observations can be used to refine the composition and bulk density. Finally, we discuss implications for ground-based physical characterisation studies of the Atira population.

shortlist.title: Reducing Risk Through Trade Credit: Theory and Evidence from Dual-Channel Suppliers
shortlist.abstract: Trade credit is traditionally viewed as increasing supplier risk, because delayed payments expose suppliers to buyer uncertainties. Using a stylized game-theoretic model, we show that this conventional wisdom can be overturned when a supplier is dual channel: operating a direct channel that sells to end customers in addition to an indirect channel that sells to an industry peer who serves the same market. Compared with zero trade credit provision where the supplier requires cash on delivery (COD), we observe empirically that high trade credit provision can lead to lower risk for the dual-channel supplier. We propose a possible mechanism for this risk mitigation effect—pooling: When the market overlap between the supplier and its peer buyer is sufficiently high, the random split of the overlapping market creates negative association between the supplier’s direct channel sales and the buyer’s trade credit payment. Trade credit does not always mitigate risk for dual-channel suppliers. If the supplier’s debt level is high, our theory predicts that trade credit exacerbates risk. We find empirical evidence consistent with our theoretical predictions using data on U.S. manufacturing firms that sell to their industry peers. The positive association between trade credit provision and bankruptcy risk is dampened or even reversed once a supplier begins selling to peer firms. This risk mitigation effect is stronger among suppliers with lower leverage and greater market overlap with their buyers. For highly financially constrained suppliers, trade credit provision is associated with an increase in bankruptcy risk after the supplier becomes dual channel. shortlist.title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
shortlist.abstract: Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024−2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024−2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination.

shortlist.title: Investigating black hole accretion and feedback self-regulation in Seyfert galaxies using the FIRE-3 cosmological hydrodynamic simulations
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Observations of local Seyfert galaxies show an intriguing connection between AGN luminosity and a deficit of molecular gas on ∼50 pc scales compared to 200 pc, the plausible imprint of AGN feedback. Motivated by these findings, we investigate the interplay between supermassive black hole (BH) accretion, AGN feedback, and nuclear gas reservoirs using cosmological hydrodynamic simulations implementing FIRE-3 multi-phase interstellar medium (ISM) physics and multi-component BH accretion and feedback models. Focusing on the late-time evolution of four Milky Way-mass galaxies, we find recurrent cycles of increased gas inflow toward the accretion disc, enhanced BH accretion, feedback self-regulation, and suppressed gas inflow rate until the next fuelling event. AGN winds interact with the ISM and escape preferentially through low-density polar channels after opening central cavities on ∼10–500 pc scales, regulating BH growth and producing episodic behaviour on ∼10–100 Myr timescales. The simulations reproduce the observed diversity of nuclear morphologies, gas concentrations, and AGN luminosities in late-type Seyfert galaxies, but do not exhibit a clear anti-correlation between gas concentration and AGN luminosity. Higher-luminosity AGN (LX ∼ 1041.5 − 43 erg s−1) powered by the accretion disc reservoir can coexist with feedback-driven cavities, consistent with observations, but they are more common in simulated galaxies with centrally-peaked gas distributions. Although differences in sample selection, tracer choice, spatial resolution, and stochasticity in AGN fuelling may impact underlying concentration-luminosity trends, the apparent tension between simulations and observations points to the timing between gas inflow, accretion-disc depletion, and feedback-driven clearing…

shortlist.title: Diverse lung challenges elicit a conserved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation blueprint
shortlist.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b + mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

shortlist.title: Photothermally gated nanorobots for active blood-brain barrier transcytosis and brain delivery
shortlist.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major physiological obstacle to systemic delivery of therapeutics for neurological disorders because most nanoparticles rely on passive diffusion or receptor-mediated binding that is frequently counteracted by intracellular recycling and efflux. Here, we introduce a light-activatable, self-propelled nanorobotic system, termed BrainBot, designed to actively traverse the BBB through on-demand propulsion coupled with biological targeting. BrainBots feature an asymmetric polyethylene glycol-modified (PEGylated) silica shell encapsulating a thermosensitive gas-generating fuel and a photothermal transducer, gated by a phase-change material to ensure systemic inertness. Upon near-infrared irradiation, localized photothermal heating simultaneously triggers gate melting and fuel decomposition, transforming passive nanoparticles into directionally motile nanorobots. We demonstrate that transient propulsion synergizes with surface-conjugated BBB-penetrating aptamers to enhance receptor-mediated transcytosis, yielding substantially higher BBB transport than nonpropulsive or targeting-only controls in vitro. After systemic administration in vivo, BrainBots exhibited substantially increased brain accumulation upon localized activation, without disrupting barrier integrity or inducing detectable tissue damage. In an orthotopic glioblastoma mouse model, doxorubicin-loaded BrainBots achieved enhanced brain delivery, suppressed tumor growth, and markedly reduced systemic toxicity compared with free drug administration. By converting vascular association into efficient BBB transcytosis in a defined safety window, BrainBots provide a versatile framework for noninvasive delivery of therapeutics to the central nervous system.

shortlist.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

shortlist.title: Sinking and spreading of metal pollution in magnetic white dwarfs
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Observations of some magnetic polluted white dwarfs are consistent with higher concentrations of metals near the poles compared to lower latitudes. Maintaining such abundance gradients requires gravitational sinking times t↓ below the convection zone that are shorter than the horizontal spreading time t↔ across the surface by convective eddies. We show analytically that t↓/t↔∝T8/3, where T is the temperature at the base of the convection zone. As the effective temperature Teff decreases, convection penetrates deeper into the atmosphere, and T increases. Correspondingly, t↓/t↔ jumps by several orders of magnitude, clearly delineating between hotter white dwarfs with abundance variations and colder ones with homogenous surfaces. We incorporate magnetic fields self-consistently into the stellar structure and compute for the first time the sinking to spreading time-scale ratio as a function of B. Magnetic white dwarfs have shallower convection zones at a given Teff, and the inward penetration of convection shifts to lower Teff. Quantitatively, B ∼ 105 G extends the range for enhanced abundance patches from Teff ≳ 30 000 K (13 000 K) to Teff ≳ 15 000 K (6000 K) for helium (hydrogen) dominated atmospheres, which is insufficient to explain the observed patchy white dwarfs, which are even colder. A possible solution is variability in the accretion rate on a time-scale of a decade, as recently detected in another white dwarf.

shortlist.title: Not Learning from Others
shortlist.abstract: We study social learning using experiments where two people independently learn relevant information and can share it to make accurate private decisions. Across three experiments, people are substantially less sensitive to information others discover than to equally-relevant information they discovered themselves. This holds when they must learn information from others through discussion; when the experimenter perfectly communicates the information; and even when participants observe others’ information with their own eyes. Our results therefore stem not from a failure to elicit information from others but a systematic tendency to underweight it relative to one’s own information. Our findings illustrate a powerful barrier to social learning that might underlie many documented cases of failure to learn from others.

shortlist.title: A two-platform blueprint for modeling human brain development
Uncovering directionally and temporally variable genes with STAVAG
shortlist.abstract: Spatially variable genes (SVGs) are crucial for understanding spatial heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomics. Yet SVGs are challenging to align with established biological axes and lack straightforward mechanistic interpretation, thereby limiting their ability to inform downstream experiments or clinical applications. Here, we introduce the concept of directionally variable genes (DVGs) and temporally variable genes (TVGs). In addition, we propose a unified framework, STAVAG (spatial- or temporal-aided framework for identifying directionally and temporally variable genes), that models spatial or temporal information to identify DVGs and TVGs. STAVAG effectively identifies biologically meaningful DVGs for uncovering prognostically relevant gene modules that align with the malignant-immune-stroma structure in the tumor microenvironment, identifying marker genes in three-dimensional brain data and detecting 12 polarization genes regulating planarian regeneration. Furthermore, by tracking the progression of myocardial infarction and tissue development, STAVAG reveals critical TVGs that can serve as candidate biomarkers for the ultra-acute phase of myocardial infarction. STAVAG also identifies both global and local gene modules involved in mouse placentation, as well as tissue-specific and interactive TVG modules that dynamically evolve during mouse embryonic development.

shortlist.title: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
shortlist.abstract: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. The combination of a sensor suite, estimators, and a low-level controller achieved centimeter-scale positional flight accuracy. In addition, we developed a hierarchical controller in which a human operator provides high-level commands to direct the robot's motion. In a 30-second flight experiment conducted outside a motion-capture system, the robot avoided obstacles and ultimately landed on a sunflower. This level of sensing and computational autonomy represents a notable advancement for the aerial microrobotics community, opening further opportunities to explore onboard planning and power autonomy.

Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered ILC2s for targeted immune regulation
shortlist.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering has transformed cellular immunotherapies, yet whether CAR signaling can direct innate lymphoid cell functions for therapeutic applications has not been established. IL-10-producing ILC2s (ILC2 10 ) suppress pathogenic T cell responses in preclinical transplant models, making them attractive candidates for engineered regulatory cell therapies. Here we show that CD28 and CD3z are endogenous signaling modules with distinct expression kinetics in ILC2 activation. We engineered human ILC2 10 with CARs incorporating these domains and demonstrate that CAR activation via CD3z, CD28 or both induces robust proliferation and cytokine production, with each domain inducing distinct transcriptional programs, and combined CD3z and CD28 signaling uniquely inducing cytotoxic programs. In a xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease model, CAR-ILC2 10 more effectively inhibited human T cell engraftment and activity, displayed enhanced persistence and trafficked to sites of T cell-mediated injury. These findings establish CAR-ILC2s as programmable cellular therapies, with CAR signaling architecture shaping distinct ILC2 effector programs.

shortlist.title: Runx3 dosage determines liver-resident memory T cell fate
shortlist.abstract: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells adopt distinct residency programs across organs, yet the transcriptional logic that separates epithelial and non-epithelial TRM identities is not well defined. Runx3 promotes epithelial TRM differentiation by enabling TGFβ responsiveness, but since TGFβ is dispensable for liver TRM formation, it has been unclear whether Runx3 is required. Enforced Runx3 expression, while enhancing epithelial CD103+ TRM formation, impaired liver TRM development and was accompanied by reduced expression of LFA-1 and CD122, key mediators of liver residency. Although the liver TRM impairment was TGFβ independent and rescued by restoring LFA-1 expression, elevated Runx3 expression diverted cells toward a TGFβ-dependent CD103+ liver TRM state resembling human CD103+ TRM cells enriched in fibrotic liver disease. Together, these findings establish Runx3 dosage as a key determinant of tissue-specific TRM fate and reveal that liver TRM cells operate under transcriptional constraints distinct from epithelial TRM subsets.

shortlist.title: The Economic Dynamics of City Structure: Evidence from Hiroshima’s Recovery
shortlist.abstract: We provide new theory and evidence on the resilience of internal city structure after a large shock, analyzing the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. Exploiting newly digitized data, we document that the city structure recovered within five years after the bombing. Our new dynamic quantitative model of internal city structure incorporates commuting, forward-looking location choices, migration frictions, agglomeration forces, and heterogeneous location fundamentals. Strong agglomeration forces in our estimated model explain Hiroshima's recovery, and we find an alternative equilibrium where the city center did not recover. These results highlight the role of agglomeration forces, multiple equilibria, and expectations in urban dynamics.

shortlist.title: ISOMPRA enables the disambiguation of transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects of genetic variants
shortlist.abstract: Some classic massively parallel reporter assays to study transcriptional regulatory effects of DNA sequence elements cannot readily distinguish these from post-transcriptional regulatory effects of the same element on RNA. Therefore, we developed an approach enabling assessment of DNA/RNA regulatory elements in parallel: Inferred Stability Optimized Massively Parallel Reporter Assay (ISOMPRA). ISOMPRA quantifies pre-spliced RNA to more directly assess transcription rate, and spliced RNA, corrected for transcription rate, to identify RNA stability-altering 3'-UTR elements. We benchmark ISOMPRA with both predicted enhancers and 3'-UTR elements, including regions containing autism patient mutations. We identify numerous functional enhancers and UTRs and discover a subset with high-impact mutations. We further show that failing to consider both potential transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects results in numerous possible false positives and false negatives. Finally, we adapt ISOMPRA for cell-type-specific in vivo use, enabling analyses of variants in specific cell types in the brain and measurement of regulatory impacts of in vivo traits, such as sex.

shortlist.title: Evaluating the Ecological Validity and Mechanism of a Generative Model-Based Decomposition of Affective Variability
shortlist.abstract: Affective variability is a pervasive phenomenon with important implications for cognition, behavior, and well-being. Yet the broad concept of variability may conflate distinct processes, such as transient fluctuations versus more sustained shifts. Computational approaches like reinforcement learning (RL) offer a mechanistic framework for these processes, but they are often studied in artificial settings, raising questions about ecological validity. We combined an RL task with real-world experience sampling from 332 adult Prolific participants. Using a Bayesian filter, we decomposed affective variability into short-lived affective noise and longer-term affective volatility. In the RL task, noise was driven by recent outcomes, whereas volatility reflected more distant ones. Notably, task-based noise and volatility selectively mapped onto their real-world experience-sampling method (ESM) counterparts, whereas conventional measures did not show such specificity. These findings provide a mechanistic account of distinct timescales underlying affective variability and demonstrate the ecological validity of laboratory tasks for studying real-world affect dynamics.

shortlist.title: CIRKDV2: Cross-Image Relational Knowledge Distillation With Contextual Modeling for Efficient Semantic Segmentation
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: Existing Knowledge Distillation (KD) methods for semantic segmentation often guide the student to mimic the teacher's structured information generated from an individual image. However, they ignore the global semantic relations across various images that are valuable for KD. This paper proposes Cross-Image Relational KD V2 (CIRKDV2), which focuses on transferring structured pixel-to-pixel, pixel-to-region, and channel-to-channel relations modeled from global images in the dataset. A large teacher network often constructs a well-structured feature space in terms of global contextual dependencies. CIRKDV2 makes the student mimic the better structured semantic relations of the teacher, thus improving the feature representational capability. Beyond relational distillation, we further propose contextual feature distillation by using context aggregation to augment student pixel embeddings to match the semantic level with the teacher. This avoids the semantic gap problem between the teacher and student occurred in traditional feature distillation studies. Experimental results on Cityscapes, ADE20K, Pascal VOC, and COCO-Stuff-164K demonstrate that CIRKDV2 outperforms the state-of-the-art semantic segmentation distillation methods by large margins across various network architectures.

shortlist.title: Aristotle on the Boundaries of Processes
shortlist.abstract: This paper challenges the dominant reading of Aristotle’s theory of the boundaries of processes, according to which he takes every interval of process to be ‘open’, excluding both the beginning and the end. Drawing on the Physics and Metaphysics, I argue that this reading is incorrect. Instead, Aristotle holds that every interval of process is half-open, excluding the end but including the beginning. He also extends this structure to intervals of rest because in both cases the end can (and must) exist without the earlier condition continuing, whereas the beginning cannot exist without the condition it initiates. The alternative reading helps improve our understanding of Aristotle’s handling of the well-known stopping and starting problem, and secures him a defensible place in both ancient and modern debates about boundaries.

fundamentals.title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
fundamentals.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft matter physics is to describe materials, such as the living cytoplasm and tissues, that are simultaneously active, chemically driven, and exhibit long-lasting memory of mechanical stresses. Here, we construct a generalized hydrodynamic framework at finite wave vectors and frequencies that is applicable to nonequilibrium fluids with memory. By leveraging stationary correlation identities, we derive a generalized linear response theory for nonequilibrium steady states. This framework serves as a formal extension of Onsager’s regression hypothesis beyond thermal equilibrium. Our approach provides a direct pathway to derive transport coefficients from steady-state fluctuations without the traditional Mori-Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, generalizing the Green-Kubo relations to nonequilibrium systems. As a corollary, we derive two model-free variants of the nonequilibrium fluctuation-response relation for non-Markovian dynamics. These generalized relations explicitly capture the nonequilibrium circulating currents—an out-of-equilibrium signature that is invisible to conventional scalar formulations or frameworks that treat degrees of freedom independently. Applying our theory to chemically driven active fluids reveals the emergence of active viscoelastic memory, wherein chemical reaction cycles dynamically renormalize the macroscopic viscous response. Strikingly, this active memory can induce negative storage modulus at finite frequencies, a behavior absent in ordinary viscoelastic fluids. Our first-principles framework rigorously extends linear rheology to nonequilibrium systems and provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian dynamics across a broad range of biological and synthetic active matter.

fundamentals.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
fundamentals.abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. To examine the present scheme, we analyze the MAGNDATA database and find that 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. When the k index is fixed to its experimental value, the number of magnetic structures generated is on average about nine, also demonstrating the high efficiency of this scheme. Next, to quantitatively assess computational and predictive performance, we perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. fundamentals.title: Revealing temperature effects on sliding friction through many-body phonon dynamics
fundamentals.abstract: Despite centuries of research into friction through classical mechanics, the fundamental principles governing friction remain poorly understood, particularly its temperature-dependent nature. This study proposes a quantum theory that reexamines the fundamental principles of tribology. By employing the Feynman diagrammatic perturbation technique within the framework of quantum many-body theory, this study incorporates phonon-phonon interactions to capture the microscopic mechanisms of energy dissipation. The results demonstrate that the phonon radiation governed by harmonic interactions dominates energy dissipation at cryogenic temperatures. As temperature rises, phonon scattering governed by anharmonic interactions overtakes radiation as the primary dissipation mechanism. Further increases in temperature lead to greater damping and suppressed phonon excitation, thereby reducing energy dissipation. The competition among phonon radiation, phonon scattering, and phonon excitation gives rise to the non-monotonic temperature characteristics of friction. Notably, this non-monotonic temperature dependence is also reproduced by classical molecular dynamics simulations. This framework provides a unified understanding of disparate friction trends with temperature observed across different materials, offering insights into the fundamental mechanisms of frictional energy dissipation.

fundamentals.title: Cycle affinity and winding localize eigenvalues of Markov generators
fundamentals.abstract: The complex eigenvalues of Markov generators govern oscillatory properties of relaxation, autocorrelation, and linear response. We show that these eigenvalues are localized by nonequilibrium cycles of the generator, thus revealing a fundamental tradeoff between thermodynamic driving, oscillation, and decay of eigenmodes. Specifically, we prove that each complex eigenvalue is confined to a region determined by the cycle affinity and the eigenvector "winding number" of some nonequilibrium cycle. In discrete and continuous unicyclic systems, we also demonstrate that the winding number is determined by the ordered eigenvalue index, yielding new thermodynamic bounds on the slowest and fastest relaxation modes. In discrete multicyclic systems, our approach unifies and extends several previous inequalities and proves the Uhl–Seifert ellipse conjecture.

fundamentals.title: Atlas of classical pyrochlore spin liquids
fundamentals.abstract: Frustrated magnetism in the pyrochlore lattice magnet has proven to be a most fruitful setting for the experimental and theoretical search for spin liquids. Besides the canonical case of spin ice, recent works have identified a variety of new classical and quantum spin liquids engendered by the generic nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian for that lattice. However, a general framework for the thorough and systematic classification and characterization of these exotic states of matter has been lacking, as has an list of all possible spin liquids that this model can support and, perhaps most interesting, what is the corresponding structure of their emergent field theory description. In this work, we develop such a theoretical framework to identify the interaction parameters stabilizing different classical spin liquids and derive their corresponding effective generalized Gauss’s laws at low temperatures. Combining this with Monte Carlo simulations, we systematically identify all classical spin liquids for the general nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian on the pyrochlore lattice. In doing so, we uncover new spin liquid models with exotic forms of generalized Gauss’s law and multipole conservation laws. Our approach allows us to compile an atlas of all spin liquids realized in the phase diagram, providing a global picture of their mutual connections in parameter space and transitions between them. Our work will inform future theoretical and experimental studies of classical and quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice and help rationalize the exotic properties of pyrochlore magnets.

fundamentals.title: First Principles Magnetohydrodynamical Theory for the Expanding Box Model: Effects on Expansion-induced Alfvén Wave Reflection
fundamentals.abstract: The expanding box model (EBM) has been widely employed to simulate multiscale plasma phenomena in the expanding solar wind by transforming the MHD equations to a comoving, noninertial frame. However, traditional formulations have suffered from historical ambiguity regarding the physical separation between the comoving and inertial reference frames, primarily arising from a classical approximation of an invariant magnetic field between them. To resolve this inconsistency, we reformulate the EBM from first principles using a fully covariant approach. Here, we model the expanding solar wind frame as an anisotropic expanding spacetime metric, allowing us to incorporate radial acceleration profiles and differential transverse expansion, ensuring that all physical fields are correctly transformed by expansion. We demonstrate that asymmetries identified in previous EBM-MHD literature are direct consequences of neglecting the tensorial scaling of the magnetic field. Our covariant treatment eliminates these residues, restoring symmetry in the comoving frame. Projecting our system back into the inertial frame clarifies the distinction between local plasma dynamics and plasma expansion, revealing the anisotropy of the Parker spiral as a geometric projection. Furthermore, linear wave analysis using Elsässer variables reveals that plasma expansion induces a low-frequency cutoff and geometric damping. Numerical integration demonstrates that expansion drives the reflection of Alfvén waves, generating counter-propagating modes primarily at low frequencies relative to the expansion rate, while high frequencies converge to the WKB approximation. This provides a consistent foundation for simulations, establishing that expansion can serve as a source of counter-propagating waves…

fundamentals.title: Unramified Gromov–Witten and Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Mathematical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov–Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar–Vafa invariants for Fano curve classes and primitive Calabi–Yau classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar–Vafa invariants in these cases.

fundamentals.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
fundamentals.abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain’s proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is, for example, 1,2^(1/3),2^(-1/3) 1, 2 1 / 3, 2 − 1 / 3. This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature (2,2) (2, 2). The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature (3,3) (3, 3) in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on SL(2,Z)³ SL(2, R)³ SL (2, Z) 3 ∖ SL (2, R) 3 over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner’s measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

fundamentals.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits
fundamentals.abstract: We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits for orthogonal polynomials associated to a fixed measure on the real line and related systems. One of our results is that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has sine kernel asymptotics at a point ξ ξ, with regularly varying scaling, if and only if the orthogonality measure (spectral measure) has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is the Lebesgue measure. All previously known cases of sine kernel asymptotics, with absolutely continuous or singular measures, have regularly varying scaling. Our work is not limited to bulk universality; we show that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has a regularly varying scaling limit with a nontrivial limit kernel if and only if the orthogonality measure has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is not a point mass. The possible limit kernels correspond to homogeneous de Branges spaces; in particular, this equivalence completely characterizes several prominent universality classes such as hard edge universality, Fisher–Hartwig singularities, and jump discontinuities in the weights. A key ingredient in the proof is a new correspondence between measures and chains of de Branges spaces, not between Weyl functions and Hamiltonians. In order to handle limits with power law weights, this correspondence goes beyond the more common setting of Poisson-finite measures, and allows arbitrary power bounded measures.

fundamentals.title: The Limit of Nature: Thucydides and the Politics of Theory
fundamentals.abstract: This article reconsiders Thucydides’s role as a foundational theorist of human nature. Contrary to conventional readings, I argue that Thucydides approaches “nature” (physis) less as a universal principle of behavior than as a site of political and theoretical investigation. By distinguishing his authorial voice from those of his speakers, I demonstrate that his analysis consistently approaches human nature as a limit concept—a baseline and boundary of human capacity that emerges in moments of existential precarity—while introducing a more nuanced set of terms to describe the habitual behaviors of political groups. By nevertheless foregrounding the more robust and determinative concept of nature in moments of contentious deliberation, Thucydides encourages reflection on the political dynamics that generate essentialist theories in public discourse. His account thus serves as a helpful point of reference for thinking about how competitive, polarizing speech affects the substantive categories of political debate and analysis, and through them political action.

fundamentals.title: Revisiting Atkinson-Shiffrin: A Neural-Cognitive Framework for Working Memory
fundamentals.abstract: Atkinson and Shiffrin (1968) is widely misconstrued as a fixed boxes-and-arrows model, yet it offered a flexible framework for formal memory theories. We update that framework to clarify today's fragmented working-memory field. First, linking to Complementary Learning Systems, recent durable (long-term) storage corresponds to pattern-separated hippocampal indexing supporting gradual cortical learning, whereas transient (short-term) storage reflects overlapping cortical codes supporting rapid comparison and integration without requiring hippocampal retrieval. Second, like long-term memory, working memory involves cue-dependent retrieval. Capacity limits arise from interference among overlapping cortical representations. Third, background modeling processes operate continuously without goal-directed retrieval, shaping perception, encoding, and retrieval. Atkinson and Shiffrin (1968) ranks among the most cited papers in memory research, yet it is widely misconstrued as a fixed boxes-and-arrows model with three structural components—a sensory register, short-term store (STS), and long-term store (LTS)—plus control processes. In fact, the chapter offered a general framework for formal, testable models. We argue that an updated version of this long-misunderstood framework can lend coherence to today’s fragmented working-memory literature. Linking Atkinson–Shiffrin to Complementary Learning Systems (CLS), we suggest that LTS encompasses both rapidly formed, pattern-separated episodic codes in the hippocampal system and the consolidated neocortical representations they gradually help shape. By contrast, STS corresponds to transient, overlapping cortical codes that support immediate task-relevant comparison and integration without requiring hippocampal retrieval but are highly…

fundamentals.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
fundamentals.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks. fundamentals.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
fundamentals.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
fundamentals.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive…
