fundamentals.title: Constructive Ordinal Exponentiation
fundamentals.abstract: In classical mathematics, ordinal arithmetic is well-studied; constructively, addition and multiplication are well-known. We study constructive ordinal exponentiation, where ordinals are taken to be transitive, extensional, and wellfounded orders on sets. We present a negative result showing that general constructive ordinal exponentiation is impossible, but we suggest two definitions that come close. The first definition is abstract and solely motivated by the expected equations; this works as long as the base of the exponential is positive. The second definition is based on decreasing lists and can be seen as a constructive version of Sierpiński’s definition via functions with finite support; this requires the base to have a trichotomous least element. Whenever it makes sense to ask the question, the two constructions are equivalent, allowing us to prove algebraic laws, cancellation properties, and preservation of decidability of the exponential. The core ideas do not depend on any specific constructive set theory or type theory, but a concrete computer-checked mechanization using the Agda proof assistant is given in homotopy type theory.

fundamentals.title: Decoding Direct Regeneration of Spent LiFePO 4: From Defect Evolution to Thermodynamic–Kinetic Barrier Engineering
fundamentals.abstract: The rapid growth of LiFePO 4 (LFP) batteries has made the sustainable recycling of spent cathodes increasingly important for the battery circular economy. Direct regeneration has emerged as the most promising strategy because it preserves the pristine framework, minimizes energy consumption, and maximizes material value. However, the underlying principles governing regeneration remain elusive, as exemplified by the apparent thermodynamic‐kinetic paradox that metallic lithium has been reported to be ineffective for restoring spent LFP, whereas weaker reductants can achieve effective recovery. These observations indicate that regeneration is governed not by thermodynamic driving force alone, but by the coupled effects of electron transfer, ion diffusion, and lattice defects. In this study, we introduce a multiscale defect framework that correlates defect formation energy (Δ H f), migration barriers (E a), and electron‐transfer reorganization energy (λ) with different degradation states of spent LFP. A hypothesis that the dominant barrier evolves with degradation was proposed, enabling failure‐dependent strategies ranging from relithiation and phase‐boundary engineering to defect‐guided upcycling. By transforming regeneration from empirical optimization into rational barrier engineering, this perspective provides a unified understanding of diverse restoration pathways. Finally, emerging challenges, including impurity management, AI‐assisted diagnostics, and closed‐loop materials design, are discussed to guide the development of sustainable battery recycling technologies.

fundamentals.title: Temperature-dependent kinetic isotope effects in methane reactions with OH and Cl reshape atmospheric sink fractionation
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: The abundances of stable isotopes in methane (CH 4) are used to distinguish fossil and biological emissions and to constrain the global methane budget. While these analyses require correction for isotopic fractionation occurring in methane’s atmospheric reactions, the temperature dependence of the kinetic isotope effects (KIEs) are poorly described and typically ignored. Here we combine density functional theory, Møller–Plesset perturbation theory, coupled-cluster calculations, and tunneling-corrected transition state theory to develop a first-principles description of the temperature-dependent KIEs for CH 4 and its isotopologues reacting with OH and Cl over the range 100 to 500 K which exhibit substantial and previously neglected temperature dependence. Incorporation of these KIEs into the EMAC chemistry–climate model yields systematically different effective atmospheric sink fractionation factors than those obtained using temperature-invariant values. The largest differences occur for chlorine oxidation in the cold upper troposphere and stratosphere, where methane isotope budgets are particularly sensitive to reactive halogens. We find a weak 13 C–D clumping anomaly and a strong D–D clumping anomaly, confirming earlier work and demonstrating that atmospheric oxidation produces substantial enrichment in Δ 12 CH 2 D 2, and helping to reconcile source signatures with atmospheric observations. These results show that temperature-dependent KIEs are required for robust interpretation of methane isotopes in both contemporary and past atmospheres.

fundamentals.title: Coverage Effects in Heterogeneous Catalysis: From Fundamental Understanding to Predictive Modeling
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
authors: Danish Uzair Bin Abdul Hamid Khan Surattee
fundamentals.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calculations suffer from vast combinatorial complexity on crowded surfaces, while machine learning methods require large training data sets and have limited physical interpretability. We reveal a physics-based linear correlation mapping complex coverage-dependent adsorption energies directly to computationally inexpensive gas-phase pairwise interactions that are evaluated via Mie potentials. This correlation is governed by bond order conservation: as surface−adsorbate interactions weaken under crowding, adsorbate−adsorbate interactions strengthen. This correlation generalizes across metal surfaces having diverse crystal facets, surface tensions, and single- and multicomponent adsorption classes (e.g., dissociative S*, N* + O*, and nondissociative CO*). This correlation predicts coverage-dependent reaction thermodynamics for NO* dissociation and for atomic-adsorbate diffusion. Coverage-dependent trends in adsorption energies of CO*/Pt(111) agree with experimental calorimetry. Ultimately, these gas-phase pairwise interactions are a descriptor for lateral interactions of atomic and structurally simple adsorbates on structurally stable metal surfaces. The generalizability and physical interpretability of this descriptor open new avenues for modeling adsorption and reaction energies on crowded metal surfaces.

fundamentals.title: Turnovers Drive Supported Metal Nanoparticle Catalyst Surface Reconstruction to Kinetically Trapped Metastable Structures
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Supported metal catalysts often operate with high adsorbate coverages that can alter nanoparticle structures as compared to the clean catalyst. Such restructuring is typically described within an equilibrium picture that assumes that nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages adopt their thermodynamically preferred state. Here, we challenge this assumption and propose that under conditions of high adsorbate coverage and fast turnovers of surface species, supported metal nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages can become kinetically trapped in metastable states. We studied CO adsorption–desorption quasi-equilibrium on Pt/γ-Al2O3 using in situ IR spectroscopy and chemisorption as a function of temperature (300–650 K), CO pressure (10–2–10–4 bar), and visible photon flux (0–2 W cm–2 440 nm photons). The adsorbed CO IR band area increases with temperature and photon flux, contrary to equilibrium predictions of decreasing coverage. Estimates of apparent Pt dispersion and CO desorption rates, along with the reversibility of IR spectral changes, support the hypothesis that when CO turnovers are faster than Pt atomic rearrangements to their equilibrium state, the catalyst is driven into metastable states. We estimate atomic rearrangements time scales of 10–1–10–3 s on CO-covered Pt nanoparticles at ∼500–600 K. Grand-canonical sampling calculations show that equilibrium Pt–CO structures cannot reproduce the experimental IR trends, implying the presence of off-equilibrium coverages, structures, or both. By matching the experimental trend, theory identifies a plausible flat, nonequilibrium free-energy region that can facilitate kinetic trapping of metastable catalyst states. These results highlight the need for theoretical and experimental approaches targeting…

fundamentals.title: Uncovering directionally and temporally variable genes with STAVAG
fundamentals.abstract: Spatially variable genes (SVGs) are crucial for understanding spatial heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomics. Yet SVGs are challenging to align with established biological axes and lack straightforward mechanistic interpretation, thereby limiting their ability to inform downstream experiments or clinical applications. Here, we introduce the concept of directionally variable genes (DVGs) and temporally variable genes (TVGs). In addition, we propose a unified framework, STAVAG (spatial- or temporal-aided framework for identifying directionally and temporally variable genes), that models spatial or temporal information to identify DVGs and TVGs. STAVAG effectively identifies biologically meaningful DVGs for uncovering prognostically relevant gene modules that align with the malignant-immune-stroma structure in the tumor microenvironment, identifying marker genes in three-dimensional brain data and detecting 12 polarization genes regulating planarian regeneration. Furthermore, by tracking the progression of myocardial infarction and tissue development, STAVAG reveals critical TVGs that can serve as candidate biomarkers for the ultra-acute phase of myocardial infarction. STAVAG also identifies both global and local gene modules involved in mouse placentation, as well as tissue-specific and interactive TVG modules that dynamically evolve during mouse embryonic development.

fundamentals.title: Curvature-guided chiral collective organization of myoblast tissues
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Surface curvature is a fundamental geometric cue in tissue morphogenesis, yet its role in guiding collective cell organization has remained elusive. Here, we show that curvature acts as a geometric control parameter that shapes supracellular alignment and chirality while modulating myogenic differentiation in myoblast tissues. Cells cultured on curved substrates self-organize into robust helical assemblies whose handedness is set, and can be reversed, by the sign of curvature: convex fibers produce right-handed helices, whereas concave channels invert the chirality. We identify a clockwise bias in single-cell motion associated with the helical actin cytoskeleton. A minimal continuum theory coupling an effective chiral drive to curvature quantitatively captures the emergence and reversal of tissue-scale chiral alignment. On substrates with spatially varying curvature, local curvature gradients organize patterned multicellular architectures while preserving a global handedness. Curvature is also associated with myogenic state, with higher curvature linked to reduced or delayed differentiation. Together, these findings reveal how complex geometries shape the alignment, symmetry, and cellular state of living tissues.

fundamentals.title: Reducing Risk Through Trade Credit: Theory and Evidence from Dual-Channel Suppliers
fundamentals.abstract: Trade credit is traditionally viewed as increasing supplier risk, because delayed payments expose suppliers to buyer uncertainties. Using a stylized game-theoretic model, we show that this conventional wisdom can be overturned when a supplier is dual channel: operating a direct channel that sells to end customers in addition to an indirect channel that sells to an industry peer who serves the same market. Compared with zero trade credit provision where the supplier requires cash on delivery (COD), we observe empirically that high trade credit provision can lead to lower risk for the dual-channel supplier. We propose a possible mechanism for this risk mitigation effect—pooling: When the market overlap between the supplier and its peer buyer is sufficiently high, the random split of the overlapping market creates negative association between the supplier’s direct channel sales and the buyer’s trade credit payment. Trade credit does not always mitigate risk for dual-channel suppliers. If the supplier’s debt level is high, our theory predicts that trade credit exacerbates risk. We find empirical evidence consistent with our theoretical predictions using data on U.S. manufacturing firms that sell to their industry peers. The positive association between trade credit provision and bankruptcy risk is dampened or even reversed once a supplier begins selling to peer firms. This risk mitigation effect is stronger among suppliers with lower leverage and greater market overlap with their buyers. For highly financially constrained suppliers, trade credit provision is associated with an increase in bankruptcy risk after the supplier becomes dual channel. fundamentals.title: Mechanical instability generates monodisperse colloidosomes
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Formation and rupture of vesicles are fundamental processes underlying diverse phenomena in biology, materials science, and biomedical applications. Vesicles form when the area of a growing disk-like membrane reaches the instability point at which the energy barrier to the disk-to-vesicle transition vanishes. Observing such topological transitions in lipid bilayers is a challenge because of their nanoscale dimensions and rapid dynamics. We study a scaled-up model of membranes assembled from rod-shaped colloidal particles. The unique features of colloidal membranes enable the real-time visualization of spontaneous vesicle closure driven by an instability arising from competition between edge and bending energies that is universal to all membrane-based materials. A continuum theory with independently measured material parameters quantitatively predicts the instability point for vesicle formation and intermediate membrane conformations during the disk-to-vesicle transition. The instability generates monodisperse, selectively permeable colloidosomes whose size is controlled by gravity and membrane elasticity, providing a scalable and programmable platform for diverse applications.

fundamentals.title: Optimal Inapproximability of Satisfiable k-LIN over Non-Abelian Groups
fundamentals.abstract: A seminal result of Håstad [19] shows that for k ≥ 3, it is NP-hard to find an assignment that satisfies 1/|G|+ε fraction of the constraints of a given k -LIN instance over an abelian group, even if there is an assignment that satisfies (1 − ε) fraction of the constraints, for any constant ε > 0. Engebretsen, Holmerin, and Russell [14] later showed that the same hardness result holds for k -LIN instances over any finite non-abelian group. Unlike the abelian case, where we can efficiently find a solution if the instance is satisfiable, in the non-abelian case, it is NP-complete to decide if a given system of linear equations is satisfiable or not, as shown by Goldmann and Russell [16]. Surprisingly, for certain non-abelian groups G, given a satisfiable k -LIN instance over G, one can in fact do better than just outputting a random assignment using a simple but clever algorithm. The approximation factor achieved by this algorithm varies with the underlying group. In this paper, we show that this algorithm is optimal by proving a tight hardness of approximation of a satisfiable k -LIN instance over any non-abelian G, assuming P ≠ NP. As a corollary, we also get 3-query probabilistically checkable proofs with perfect completeness over large alphabets with improved soundness. Our proof crucially uses structural properties captured by Gowers’ notion of quasi-randomness for non-abelian groups [17].

fundamentals.title: STIR: Reed–Solomon Proximity Testing with Fewer Queries
fundamentals.abstract: We present STIR (Shift To Improve Rate), an interactive oracle proof of proximity (IOPP) for Reed–Solomon codes that achieves the best known query complexity of any concretely efficient IOPP for this problem. For λ bits of security, STIR has query complexity O (log d + λ ⋅ loglog d), while FRI, a popular protocol, has query complexity O (λ ⋅ log d) (including variants of FRI based on conjectured security assumptions). STIR relies on a new technique for recursively improving the rate of the tested Reed–Solomon code. We provide an implementation of STIR compiled to a SNARK. Compared to a highly-optimized implementation of FRI, STIR achieves an improvement in argument size that ranges from 1.25× to 2.46× depending on the chosen parameters, with similar prover and verifier running times. For example, in order to achieve 128 bits of security for degree 2 26 and rate 1/4, STIR has argument size 114 KiB, compared to 211 KiB for FRI.

fundamentals.title: Aristotle on the Boundaries of Processes
fundamentals.abstract: This paper challenges the dominant reading of Aristotle’s theory of the boundaries of processes, according to which he takes every interval of process to be ‘open’, excluding both the beginning and the end. Drawing on the Physics and Metaphysics, I argue that this reading is incorrect. Instead, Aristotle holds that every interval of process is half-open, excluding the end but including the beginning. He also extends this structure to intervals of rest because in both cases the end can (and must) exist without the earlier condition continuing, whereas the beginning cannot exist without the condition it initiates. The alternative reading helps improve our understanding of Aristotle’s handling of the well-known stopping and starting problem, and secures him a defensible place in both ancient and modern debates about boundaries.

food.title: Functional feed additive intervention strategies for necrotic enteritis in broiler chickens: a perspective on host–pathogen interactions and the gut microbiota
food.abstract: Necrotic enteritis (NE) threatens intestinal health and productivity in broiler chickens, prompting growing interest in nutritional interventions amid restrictions on in-feed antibiotic use. NE pathogenesis involves Clostridium perfringens (C. perfringens) virulence, mucosal injury, and alterations in the gut microbiota and its metabolic environment, processes that may interact to influence disease progression. Centered on host-pathogen interactions, this review proposes an integrative framework for examining NE pathogenesis and identifying potential targets for nutritional intervention. We synthesize evidence from experimental NE models evaluating phytogenic additives, probiotics, prebiotics, organic acids, functional amino acids, feed enzymes, and multi-component formulations. We compare their effects on pathogen-associated processes, intestinal mucosal integrity, immune and inflammatory responses, and gut microbial communities, and assess how these changes relate to intestinal lesions, mortality, and growth performance. Intervention efficacy varies with additive composition, dose, and challenge conditions. Importantly, improvements in barrier-related, immunological, and microbial indicators do not consistently translate into protection against NE or improved growth, and the relative contributions of proposed mechanisms remain uncertain. Future studies should more directly connect functional and mechanistic evidence with disease and production outcomes and evaluate the reproducibility of protective effects, production benefits, and economic feasibility of defined formulations across challenge models and commercial production settings. Such evidence will support the rational selection and integration of nutritional interventions into comprehensive NE control…

food.title: “Prevalence and associated risk factors of ectoparasite infestation in Ethiopian poultry: meta-analysis”
food.abstract: Ectoparasite infestation is a major parasitic problem affecting chicken health and productivity worldwide. Despite the substantial economic impact of poultry ectoparasites, evidence on their epidemiology in Ethiopia remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of ectoparasite infestation, characterise major ectoparasite groups, and assess associated factors among chickens in Ethiopia. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2026. Seventeen articles met the inclusion criteria, yielding 56 datasets, as some studies reported multiple ectoparasite groups. A random-effects model was used to estimate pooled prevalence while accounting for between-study heterogeneity. The overall pooled prevalence of ectoparasite infestation among chickens in Ethiopia was 63.0% (95% CI: 53.0-73.0%). In terms of region, the highest prevalence was observed in Oromia (68.0%), followed by Tigray (63.0%) and SNNPR (58.0%), whereas Amhara showed the lowest prevalence (42.0%). Among the reported ectoparasite groups, lice had the highest pooled prevalence (43.0%), followed by mites (27.0%), fleas (26.0%), mixed infestations (9.0%), and ticks (6.0%). The prevalence of ectoparasite infestation showed a slight decreasing trend over time, but the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.431). While prevalence was similar between studies with sample sizes ≤384 and >384, no significant difference was observed between the groups (p = 0.906). Furthermore, Subgroup analysis evaluated breed, sex, age, and management system as potential associated factors; however, none demonstrated a statistically significant association with ectoparasite…

food.title: Carbon-smart broiler production: life-cycle hotspots, mitigation strategies, and meat-quality trade-offs
food.abstract: The poultry industry faces mounting pressure to reduce its environmental footprint while maintaining high productivity, economic viability, and superior meat quality. Although broiler production generally yields lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions than other livestock sectors, its rapid global expansion has heightened concerns over the carbon emissions associated with feed production, energy use, manure management, housing, transportation, and processing. As a result, integrated carbon-smart strategies are essential for achieving sustainable poultry systems. This review critically evaluates the primary contributors to the carbon footprint of broiler production and synthesizes current and emerging mitigation strategies that do not compromise productive performance or meat quality. We place particular emphasis on precision nutrition-including low-protein and precision-formulated diets-alternative protein sources, phytogenic feed additives, precision feeding technologies, resource-efficient housing, renewable energy integration, and circular bioeconomy approaches. Furthermore, we examine how these mitigation strategies influence key meat quality attributes, such as oxidative stability, fatty acid composition, shelf life, and sensory characteristics. Recent advances in precision livestock farming, AI-driven decision support systems, and sustainability-oriented breeding are also highlighted as promising tools for enhancing carbon efficiency. Finally, we address current challenges in carbon footprint quantification, notably methodological inconsistencies in life cycle assessments (LCA) and the lack of standardized sustainability indicators for the poultry sector. By integrating nutritional, managerial, technological, and environmental perspectives, this review proposes a…

food.title: Molecular characterization and immunoprotective efficacy of two Eimeria tenella surface antigens in chickens
food.abstract: Eimeria tenella causes cecal coccidiosis in chickens, leading to substantial economic losses to the poultry industry. Surface antigens (SAGs) mediate host‑parasite attachment and invasion. Although several SAGs have been characterized as vaccine candidates, the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of EtSAG7 and EtSAG10 remain unknown. In this study, the genes encoding EtSAG7 and EtSAG10 were cloned for recombinant protein expression, and corresponding DNA vaccines were also constructed. Their expression across different developmental stages of E. tenella was examined, revealing that both antigens are present in sporozoites, merozoites, and microgametes-marking the first detection of SAGs in the sexual stage. The immunoprotective efficacy of both vaccine forms was evaluated in 14‑day‑old chickens. Transcription and expression in chicken muscle were confirmed by RT‑PCR and western blotting. Vaccinated chickens exhibited significantly higher cytokine and IgY antibody levels than controls, with IFN‑γ and TNF‑α induced by rEtSAG10 significantly higher than by rEtSAG7. All vaccinated groups showed reduced oocyst output (p < 0.05), alleviated cecal lesions (p < 0.05), and higher weight gains, with anticoccidial index (ACI) values all exceeding 160. Both recombinant proteins and DNA vaccines derived from EtSAG7 and EtSAG10 conferred significant protection against E. tenella, with EtSAG10 inducing stronger Th1 immune responses. Together with their multi‑stage expression profile-including the first detection in the sexual stage-these findings establish EtSAG7 and EtSAG10 as promising broad‑spectrum vaccine candidates for the development of novel vaccines against avian coccidiosis.

food.title: The role of ethanol in the perception of beverages: Sensory, physicochemical and oral processing perspectives
food.abstract: Background Non-alcoholic and low-alcohol (NoLo) beverages have experienced rapid growth in recent years, driven by evolving societal expectations towards healthier lifestyles. However, reducing ethanol content remains a major formulation challenge, as ethanol plays multiple roles in beverage perception. Beyond its psychoactive effects, ethanol is a sensorially active molecule, contributing to olfactory, gustatory and trigeminal sensations, while also acting as a key physicochemical component that structures the beverage matrix and modulates aroma compound release. Scope and approach This review synthesises current knowledge on the role of ethanol in the sensory perception of alcoholic and NoLo beverages from sensory, physicochemical, and oral processing perspectives. Key findings and conclusion Changes in ethanol concentration not only alter the perception of ethanol itself, but also influence the perception of other sensory attributes, particularly aroma, through retention and partitioning effects that generally favour greater aroma release in low- or no-alcohol matrices. However, ethanol-related effects on salivary properties and oral-processing mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Current evidence remains insufficient to establish clear mechanistic relationships, although the limited current knowledge shows a potential role of alcohol in modulating aroma-protein interactions during oral processing. By integrating these complementary perspectives, this review highlights key mechanisms underlying ethanol’s contribution to beverage perception and identifies critical knowledge gaps. Advancing this mechanistic understanding is essential for the rational development of NoLo beverages that preserve sensory quality and consumer acceptance.

food.title: Essential oils in food preservation: Integrating antimicrobial efficacy with evolutionary and microbiome selectivity considerations
authors: Eliza de Jesus Barros dos Santos
food.abstract: Background Essential oils (EOs) and their constituents (EOCs) can support food preservation, but antimicrobial efficacy alone does not characterize every surviving-cell state or community response. Minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations, colony-forming units, and shelf-life measurements remain essential; additional endpoints may be needed when exposure histories or non-target populations are relevant. Scope and approach This critical narrative review integrates foundational and recent studies on EO/EOC exposure, microbial stress responses, experimental evolution, loss of culturability, and food microbial communities. Evidence is distinguished by intervention, experimental system, exposure design, and endpoint. Laboratory and non-food findings are used for mechanistic context, with their transfer to foods explicitly limited. Key findings and conclusions Reported responses include injury, altered stress tolerance, stable resistance in selected experimental systems, cross-protection, collateral sensitivity, and viable but nonculturable (VBNC) states; other studies detected no increased tolerance under the conditions tested. Food studies also report community and metabolite changes, although relative-abundance profiles and associations seldom establish ecological causality. We propose an integrated, evolution-aware and microbiome-selective preservation perspective organized by the Microbial Fate Map, Sublethal EO Paradox, Microbiome Selectivity Index (MSI), and Evolutionary Safety Window (ESW). MSI and ESW are proposed conceptual frameworks, without validated scores or boundaries. Their value must be tested against conventional efficacy and quality endpoints in defined food systems. Evidence for bacterial adaptation is substantially stronger than evidence for…

food.title: Emerging strategies in coffee fermentation: From starter culture to synthetic microbial community
food.abstract: Background Coffee is a globally consumed beverage. After harvesting, coffee can be processed in various ways, one of which is the wet method. The conventional wet processing method involves immersing the beans in water for fermentation. Although this fermentation improves the sensory profile of the beverage, the process is generally carried out spontaneously, relying on the indigenous microbiota, which makes standardization difficult. Scope and approach This study employed a narrative review based on articles indexed in scientific databases, including Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect, covering studies published between 2022 and 2026. This study aims to critically analyze conventionally employed fermentation processes and propose the use of synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) as an emerging strategy for this process. While many studies have investigated fermentation inoculated with isolated or mixed strains (simultaneous or sequential inoculation), there is often a lack of rational design in culture development, hindering process reproducibility. Consequently, an emerging strategy involves the rational and well-structured design of microbial communities for use in coffee fermentation. Key findings and conclusion The rational development of synthetic microbial communities, integrated with multi-omics tools, is an emerging strategy for standardizing coffee fermentation and improving beverage quality. Furthermore, the use of genetically modified organisms, either for producing compounds of interest or for specific applications, represents a promising approach to further enhance the fermentation process. Overall, the use of SynComs for coffee fermentation can be considered an emerging strategy for implementation, whereas the use of genetically…

food.title: Synergistic Effects in Hybrid Alternative Protein Systems: Mechanisms, Functional Performance, and Applications
food.journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
food.abstract: Growing concerns about the environmental impact of conventional animal protein production have accelerated the development of sustainable protein sources. Among these, hybrid alternative protein systems have attracted increasing attention because combining complementary protein sources can overcome nutritional, functional, and sensory limitations that persist in single-source alternatives. This review summarizes current knowledge on synergistic interactions in hybrid protein systems containing plant, fungal, microbial, algal, and insect-based proteins, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms underlying these effects: amino acid complementation, protein digestibility, intermolecular interactions, and the relationship between microstructure and functional properties. Recent studies have shown that strategic protein combinations, together with optimized processing conditions, can improve protein quality, solubility, emulsification, foaming, gelation, water holding capacity, texture, and sensory acceptance beyond what any single protein source achieves alone. The review further examines how extraction methods, extrusion technologies, and other structuring approaches shape hybrid protein matrices, and considers application-specific formulations spanning meat analogs, dairy alternatives, seafood substitutes, bakery products, and sports nutrition. Moreover, current challenges related to flavor, consumer acceptance, and processing approaches are discussed alongside priorities for future research. Overall, this review highlights recent advances in hybrid alternative protein systems and provides an overview of their potential for developing more nutritious, functional, and sustainable protein-based foods.

food.title: Plant-based cheese alternatives: Reframing processing strategies towards fermentation-driven innovation
food.abstract: Background The growing demand for sustainable and animal-free foods has accelerated global interest in plant-based cheese alternatives (PBCAs). Despite rapid market expansion, many commercial PBCA products still struggle to replicate the flavour, texture and functionality of dairy cheese. Key barriers include difficulty forming meltable plant protein networks, limited utilisation of plant-derived sugars by some starter cultures and a lack of suitable precursors for cheese-like flavour development. Scope and approach This review presents a process-based perspective on PBCA development by categorising current approaches into non-fermented and fermented systems. Non-fermented approaches rely mainly on functional ingredients and processing techniques to build product structure and texture, whereas fermented approaches utilise microbial metabolism to improve flavour, texture and sensory quality, with particular attention to recent advances in culture selection and adaptation. The applications and limitations of fermentation and emerging approaches, including precision fermentation, hybrid systems, multi-omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are also discussed. Key findings and conclusions Fermentation provides a promising strategy for narrowing the quality gap between plant-based and dairy cheeses. Future progress will require a better understanding of microbial adaptation to plant-based substrates and the interactions between microorganisms and plant matrices. Cultures should be evaluated in the intended cheese formulation, linking substrate utilisation and acidification with flavour and texture development. Comparisons with non-fermented controls should establish the microbial contributions, and pilot-scale trials should assess product consistency and safety. Precision…

food.title: Hydrogen-dependent sulfur and iron reduction by marine thermophiles as analogs for early Earth and ocean world processes
food.abstract: Life on the early Earth was likely anaerobic, H2 dependent, CO2 fixing, and thermophilic in a marine hydrothermal setting. Geochemical and mineral evidence suggests that sulfur and iron respiration occurred during the Paleoarchean (3.6-3.2 Ga). However, the predominant mechanisms of H2-dependent sulfur and iron respiration in hydrothermal systems, then or now, have yet to be elucidated. Studying these processes in microorganisms from modern hydrothermal systems provides context for interpreting the characteristics of life during the Paleoarchaean. All the bacteria and archaea that have been cultured and characterized as extremely thermophilic, marine, H2 dependent, and sulfur reducing or iron reducing (36 species) were surveyed for genes related to energy generation and terminal reduction processes. Respiratory hydrogenases, Nuo-like complexes, and ATP synthases were all universally conserved. These data, coupled with phenotypic and biochemical information, suggest that these organisms oxidize H2 outside the cytoplasmic membrane, reduce menaquinone, and generate a proton motive force for ATP synthesis. The most conserved sulfur reduction gene encoded a cytoplasmic NAD(P)H sulfur reductase. Genes encoding cytoplasmic hydrogenases and membrane-bound pyranopterin oxidoreductases were also common. The widespread conservation of menaquinol-dependent fumarate reductase points to CO2 assimilation as another means of electron disposal, with excess reductant possibly used to drive sulfur or iron reduction. Understanding the metabolic potential of H2-dependent marine thermophiles deepens our knowledge of life in hydrothermal systems and contributes to the interpretation of data from ocean world missions.

food.title: Tracking respiratory syncytial virus dynamics in wastewater during the 2024–2025 season in Switzerland
food.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is responsible for a substantial health burden worldwide, particularly among children and older adults. In 2023, novel immunoprophylactic interventions for RSV were approved, underscoring the need to monitor circulating RSV lineages and detect mutations that could compromise intervention effectiveness. Here, we implemented wastewater-based genomic RSV surveillance by integrating digital PCR and amplicon-based sequencing within Switzerland's national wastewater monitoring program. We tracked RSV subtypes and individual mutations across the 2024-2025 peak season in six Swiss cities. RSV-A and RSV-B co-circulated nationwide, and both exhibited similar epidemiological dynamics estimated from their subtype-specific effective reproduction numbers. No previously reported F protein mutations relevant to prophylaxis efficacy were identified. Genetic diversity analysis of wastewater-derived sequences reflected patterns previously reported in clinical data, with higher diversity in RSV-A than RSV-B, and greater variability in the G compared to the F gene. These findings demonstrate the potential of wastewater-based RSV surveillance for monitoring RSV dynamics and diversity and establish a national baseline for RSV evolution during the first season following vaccine implementation in Switzerland.IMPORTANCERespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory virus that can cause serious illness in vulnerable populations. The recent development of RSV immunoprophylaxis products has increased the importance of monitoring viral evolution. Standard surveillance based on clinical testing captures only a fraction of infections. Our findings demonstrate that wastewater-based genomic surveillance, using regularly collected samples throughout the peak…

food.title: Exploration of the microbial diversity and functional characteristics of traditional sourdough in Inner Mongolia
food.abstract: To explore the microbial diversity and metabolic functional characteristics of traditional sourdough in Inner Mongolia, 40 samples were analysed using culturable methods and metagenomic sequencing. A total of 353 bacterial isolates were identified and belonged to 30 genera and 50 species using culturable methods, with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum , Leuconostoc citreum , Lactococcus lactis , Pediococcus pentosaceus , and Fructilactobacillus sanfranciscensis being the dominant species. Furthermore, 225 yeast isolates belonging to 9 genera and 11 species were identified, among which Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Maudiozyma humilis were predominant. A total of 3,698 taxa across 1,114 genera were annotated using metagenomic sequencing, and the dominant species were consistent with the results obtained using the culture method. Microbial diversity analysis confirmed significant disparities in community composition between continuously back-slopped and spontaneously fermented sourdough ( p < 0.05). Successive back-slopping remarkably enriched niche-specialized, sourdough-adapted microbial taxa, whereas spontaneous fermentation maintained a more complex microbiome abundant in flour-derived plant-associated bacteria. Metagenomic functional annotation indicated that lactic acid bacteria and yeasts synergistically regulate core fermentative pathways, including carbohydrate catabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, and CO 2 generation for dough leavening. Ultimately, this study provides a comprehensive characterization of the microbial diversity and functional potential of traditional sourdough from Inner Mongolia and contributes valuable regional data and a cultured isolate collection, supporting further applied research and the development of standardized starter cultures for…

Comparative transcriptomics reveals the electrosynthesis mechanisms of Sporomusa ovata under different reduction potentials
food.abstract: Understanding the metabolic mechanism of Sporomusa ovata is crucial for the practical applications of microbial electrosynthesis systems (MESs), a promising technology to sequester CO2. This study aims to investigate the electrosynthesis mechanisms of S. ovata under different cathodic potentials using comparative transcriptomics. As the cathodic potential became more negative from -0.4 to -0.7 V (vs standard hydrogen electrode [SHE]), acetate synthesis in MESs increased from 0.59 ± 0.05 to 6.03 ± 0.23 mM, while electron recovery efficiency decreased from 117.7 ± 6.8% to 52.5 ± 2.4%. Transcriptional analysis revealed that H2-mediated indirect extracellular electron uptake may be the core mechanism of S. ovata at -0.7 and -0.4 V. At both potentials, S. ovata relied on ATP synthesis from membrane hydrogenase-dependent respiratory chains. Compared with -0.4 V, upregulation of hydABC at -0.7 V enhanced cytoplasmic hydrogenase-based reducing power, dominating CO2 fixation via the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. Compared with -0.7 V, the transcriptional activity of membrane hydrogenase (hupSL, hydA2B2) and higher expression of membrane electron transport components reflected the importance of the membrane-bound respiratory chain for S. ovata survival at -0.4 V. This work provides strategies for fine-tuning MESs to optimize energy efficiency and product specificity in sustainable biomanufacturing.IMPORTANCEMicrobial electrosynthesis (MES) is a promising CO2 sequestration technology and contributes to climate mitigation. food.title: Development and behavior of Steinernema hermaphroditum nematodes are impacted by a bacterial flavin monooxygenase
food.abstract: Beneficial animal-microbe symbioses occur across the tree of life, with observable impacts on animal development and behavior. The bacterial enzyme complex HpaBC hydroxylates aromatic compounds, which may effect host neurotransmitter-dependent phenotypes. The bacterium Xenorhabdus griffiniae, a beneficial intestinal symbiont of Steinernema hermaphroditum entomopathogenic nematodes, encodes HpaBC. Computational docking of X. griffiniae HpaB substrates showed energetically favorable docking for 4-hydroxyphenylacetate and tyrosine and some affinity for dopamine. We hypothesized that Xenorhabdus HpaBC may influence nematode host development or behavior through its potential action on tyrosine degradation or dopamine catabolism. In support of this idea, we demonstrate a negative correlation between X. griffiniae hpaBC expression and body length and egg-laying behavior in adult S. hermaphroditum nematodes. Moreover, hpaBC expression is necessary for X. griffiniae bacteria to colonize the nematode intestine in the infective juvenile stage. Taken together, these findings indicate that HpaBC may be a part of the metabolic crosstalk occurring between X. griffiniae and S. hermaphroditum at multiple stages of their shared life cycle. hpaBC orthologs are widely present across bacterial phyla, including in pathogens and mutualists of plants and animals. food.title: Microbiological safety of retail black pepper (Piper nigrum L.): Integrated culture-dependent and 16S rRNA metabarcoding characterization of bacterial contamination
food.abstract: Black pepper ( Piper nigrum L.) is the most consumed spice and of greatest economic relevance in the world, however, it is also a vehicle for foodborne microorganisms, especially because it is frequently used without additional heat treatment. This study investigated the microbiological quality and the microbiome of retail black pepper, integrating culture-dependent methods, molecular identification of cultivable isolates and metabarcoding of the 16S rRNA gene. A total of 100 samples was analyzed regarding the presence of Enterobacterales, Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. Enterobacterales were detected in 82% of the samples, E. coli in 11% and Salmonella spp. in 3%. Among the Enterobacterales, the most incident genera were Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Cronobacter, Kosakonia and Pluralibacter . Potentially pathogenic species were identified, including Klebsiella pneumoniae, Cronobacter sakazakii and members of the Enterobacter cloacae complex. In addition, several species were reported for the first time in spices, such as Mixta calida and Paramixta manurensis . The metabarcoding of the 16S rRNA gene of 15 samples generated 1,301 ASVs and revealed a highly diverse bacterial community, having Clostridiaceae (26.67%), Enterobacteriaceae (26.62%) and Enterococcaceae (23.57%) as the most abundant families. The most abundant genera were Enterococcus, Clostridium sensu stricto 1, Paraclostridium, Klebsiella, Franconibacter, Lysinibacillus, Acinetobacter, Enterobacter and Cronobacter . The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to explain the reasoning of the applied black‑box machine-learning models. The machine learning models were trained to classify the level of extensiveness of the condition from the sensory attributes and physicochemical properties of the meat.3. Machine learning revealed the strongest links for husbandry condition 'genetics' (fast-growing, male-layer, dual-purpose, slower-growing) and for animal welfare (high, low) with the physicochemical and sensory quality of meat.4. The SHAP explanations showed that skin saltiness and crispiness, hardness of breast meat and meat colour b*, cooking loss, colour a* and BMORS shear energy were most important for classifying welfare. The models considered the sensory features crispiness skin, colour skin and saltiness skin and the physicochemical features colour a*, colour b* and BMORS shear energy to be most important for distinguishing between slower-growing, dual-purpose and fast-growing broilers.

food.title: Characterization of common commercial honeys across the Mediterranean area
food.abstract: This study aimed to authenticate and characterize commercial honey samples from the Mediterranean area. Seventy-two samples spanning five botanical origins (acacia, chestnut, lavender, linden, and multifloral) from five Mediterranean countries (Croatia, France, Greece, Italy, and Spain) were evaluated through melissopalynological and sensory analysis, alongside physicochemical properties, sugars, anions, and cations. Linear models were used to assess the effects of botanical and geographical origin on studied traits, while Principal Component Analysis (PCA) allowed visualize sample clustering according to them. Approximately 47% of the samples exhibited at least one non-compliance, with botanical origin mislabeling being the most prevalent issue. Following reclassification, 51 samples were retained for further analysis. Overall, 86 nectareous taxa were identified, Smilax and Citrus emerging as potential regional markers. All physicochemical parameters met European quality standards. Electrical conductivity correlated significantly with major ionic species (ρ = 0.36, p < 0.05 - 0.94, p < 0.001). Botanical origin strongly influenced honey color and ionic profiles, whereas geographical origin had a more limited effect possibly due to similarities among the sampled production areas. Pollen-based exploratory PCA clustered chestnut, acacia, and lavender honeys, mainly driven by Castanea pollen. In contrast, PCA showed no clear geographical clustering based on pollen or physicochemical data. These results suggest that combining palynological and chemical profiles can help characterize botanical origin, while geographical discrimination requires further investigation using larger and more balanced datasets.

food.title: Association analysis of KIAA0825 and SESN3 gene polymorphisms with liver performance in Landes geese
food.abstract: 1. Molecular genetic markers offer a means to improve selection efficiency in Landes geese. The objective of this study was to screen for key candidate genes and variant loci involved in the regulation of fatty liver traits in Landes geese.2. A total of 200 geese (100 males and 100 females) were subjected to an overfeeding program. Blood samples from 10 high (HWT) and 10 low liver weight (LWT) female geese were used for whole‑genome resequencing. Differential single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were identified and annotated. Validation was performed in male geese.3. Both the liver weight and liver‑to‑body-weight ratio were significantly higher in the HWT than in the LWT treatment for both sexes. Enriched pathways associated with fatty liver traits included regulation of lipolysis in adipocytes, longevity regulating pathway, axon guidance and glycerolipid metabolism.4. An SNP (T/C) was identified at the chrZ:1905252 locus of the KIAA0825 gene. In female geese, two alleles (T and C) were observed at this Z‑linked locus. The SNP of KIAA0825 was significantly associated with fatty liver weight and individuals carrying the C allele had significantly higher liver weight than those carrying the T allele (p < 0.05). No significant association was found in male geese.5. An SNP (G/A) was identified at chr1:200542695 of the sestrin 3 (SESN3) gene, with three genotypes (GG, GA, AA) present in the population. In female geese, the SESN3 SNP was significantly associated with fatty liver traits (p = 0.001) and individuals with the AA genotype had significantly higher liver weight than those with the GG genotype. In male geese, no significant association was detected.6. The sites in KIAA0825 and SESN3 can serve as candidate SNP for fatty liver traits in female Landes geese.

food.title: Effect of enrichment, stocking density and breed on feather corticosterone, feather dehydroepiandrosterone (sulphate) and their ratio in broiler chickens
food.abstract: 1. Understanding how husbandry practices affect chronic stress in broiler chickens is crucial to improve animal welfare.2. This study examined the separate and combined effects of environmental enrichment, stocking density and breed on feather corticosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone (sulphate) (DHEA(S)). These are two endocrine indicators of (long-term) stress.3. In four separate 2⨯2 factorial design experiments in Poland and two separate 2⨯2 factorial design experiments in the Netherlands, broilers with different growth rates were reared under different housing conditions. These varied in enrichment types and stocking densities, representing both conventional and less intensive conditions.4. Feather corticosterone concentrations were elevated in broilers housed without environmental enrichment and/or at higher stocking densities. However, feather corticosterone was not elevated in the faster growing breeds, but rather was lower or there was no genotype effect. The effects of enrichment, stocking density, breed and their interactions were less clear for feather DHEA(S) patterns and the corticosterone/DHEA(S) ratio.5. The results suggested that, while enrichment and stocking density clearly affected stress, the role of DHEA(S) remains complex and poorly understood.6. Further research is needed to confirm if DHEA(S) in feathers is a reliable biomarker of chronic stress in broiler chickens.

food.title: Species-dependent differences in aquaporin immunoreactivity in avian brain tissues
food.abstract: 1. Aquaporins are membrane water channel proteins that regulate cellular water transport while maintaining electrochemical gradients across cell membranes. This study investigated the expression patterns of aquaporins 1, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 11 brain tissues of Alectoris chukar, Coturnix coturnix and Gallus gallus domesticus using immunohistochemical and Western blot analyses. Astrocytic involvement was evaluated through Glial fibrillary acidic protein immunoreactivity.2. All examined Aquaporins were expressed in the brain tissues of all species, with clear species-dependent differences in expression intensity and distribution patterns. Aquaporin immunoreactivity was predominantly associated with vascular and perivascular structures across all species.3. Glial fibrillary acidic protein immunoreactivity showed a species-dependent pattern, indicating variability in astrocytic density and reactivity among the studied avian brains. The highest astrocytic involvement was observed in G. gallus domesticus, followed by A. chukar, while C. coturnix exhibited comparatively lower astrocytic reactivity. No sex-related differences were observed, which suggested that astrocytic distribution is primarily species-dependent rather than sex-dependent.4. These results showed a coordinated relationship between aquaporin expression and astrocytic architecture in the regulation of brain waterhomoeostasis. The species-specific differences reflected functional adaptations in avian neurovascular and astroglial systems.

food.title: Characterization of the metabolic plasticity of Oenococcus oeni strains as a function of the oenological matrix by untargeted exometabolomic profiling
food.abstract: Malolactic fermentation (MLF), predominantly executed by the lactic acid bacterium Oenococcus oeni, constitutes a critical process that converts L-malic acid into L-lactic acid, contributing to the microbiological stability and sensory properties of the wine. The substantial functional and genetic diversity of O. oeni gives rise to considerable metabolic heterogeneity. The objective of this study was to characterize the metabolic plasticity of eight strains of O. oeni inoculated into four red wine matrices. An analysis was conducted on the wines of Pinot Noir and Merlot, analyzed in both adjusted and unadjusted forms in terms of pH and L-malic acid concentration. To achieve this objective, we combined the monitoring of L-malic acid consumption with untargeted metabolomic profiling (LC-MS). Exometabolomic analysis enabled the mapping of metabolic variability. Although a common metabolic basis, oriented towards survival functions, was observed, distinct metabolic profiles suggest different adaptive strategies emerged between strains, particularly in the potential mobilization of central pathways and in membrane regulation or flavonoid degradation. Furthermore, oenological adjustments, regulated metabolic expression, and the nature of the matrix strongly influence the response. Polyphenols and derivatives constituted a significant proportion of the biomarkers up-regulated by all O. oeni strains. These results suggest the potential influence of the interaction between microbial genotype and wine composition on MLF outcomes. They reinforce the notion of functional plasticity in O. oeni, offering potential leverage for the customization of red wine profiles.

food.title: Non-destructive monitoring of acrylamide in air-fried biscuits: A comparative analysis of linear and non-linear machine learning models through RGB digital fingerprints
food.abstract: Acrylamide formation in baked foods is linked to the Maillard reaction, which simultaneously drives browning chromophores. This study evaluates RGB-derived chromatic fingerprints as a preliminary non-destructive screening approach for acrylamide in air-fried biscuits. High-dimensional RGB histograms were consolidated into an optimized 22-descriptor chromatic matrix. Five regression architectures were systematically evaluated: Multiple Linear Regression with Stepwise AIC, Penalized Generalized Linear Models, Partial Least Squares Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR-RBF), and Random Forest. Model performance was validated using stratified 80/20 train/test partitioning and a 500-iteration Monte Carlo cross-validation (MCCV) scheme. Non-linear architectures outperformed linear baselines, with SVR-RBF demonstrating higher predictive consistency on the independent test set (RMSEP = 19.48 μg/kg, R 2 = 0.9863; MCCV RMSEP = 23.63 ± 6.39 μg/kg). Variable importance analysis identified specific red- and blue-channel regions (R: 168-191, B: 32-55) as key chromatic drivers tracking acrylamide accumulation. Near the European Union benchmark level (350 μg/kg under Regulation (EU) 2017/2158), SVR-RBF exhibited a prediction uncertainty band of 326 – 374 μg/kg (6.8% relative uncertainty). These findings demonstrate that non-linear RGB fingerprints offer a promising proof of concept for rapid, non-destructive screening under controlled laboratory conditions. However, scaling up towards pilot and industrial implementation requires validation across a larger and more diverse sample cohort, incorporating multi-batch production and continuous processing lines under varying acquisition geometries.

food.title: Interpretable discrimination of extra virgin olive oil adulteration using NIR and FTIR spectroscopy combined with PCA-SHAP analysis
food.abstract: Extra virgin olive oil (EVOO), a high-value product of the olive oil sub-sector, is vulnerable to economically motivated adulteration, creating a need for rapid and trustworthy quality-control tools across the agri-food chain. This study developed an interpretable spectroscopic strategy for distinguishing authentic EVOO from samples adulterated with sunflower oil, refined olive oil, and olive pomace oil. Near infrared (NIR) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra were reduced by principal component analysis (PCA) and modelled using six classifiers, including decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), support vector machine (SVM), and gradient boosting machine (GBM). Model performance was evaluated using a formulation-group-held-out prediction strategy within the controlled source oil system, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, dependence plots, loading profiles, and interaction analysis were used for interpretation. The NIR-based RF model achieved the best prediction accuracy of 0.982, outperforming the best FTIR-based model with 0.821. SHAP analysis showed that the NIR model mainly relied on PC1, PC3, and PC4, which captured subtle multivariate variations across lipid-related NIR regions, indicating that the strongest absorption peaks were not necessarily the most discriminative features. In contrast, the FTIR model relied mainly on PCs associated with common triglyceride bands shared across oil categories, providing less class-specific information and partly explaining its weaker discrimination. The proposed PCA-SHAP framework supports transparent and chemically interpretable AI-based authentication of olive-derived agricultural products.
